target:
task task/fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber

Observed on a real `plan-review` workflow run against roadmap `workflow-token-reduction` (run `wf_e3402021-0af`, 2026-07-25).

The roadmap unit returned `reviewed`, so the gate cleared `needs-plan-review`. Instead of writing back the filtered original list (`cost, workflow, autonomy`), it wrote `fetch, roadmap, workflow-token-reduction` — none of which were ever tags on the item. The written values look like they were derived from the unit descriptor / fetch step rather than from the target's `tags` array, i.e. the gate agent did not actually read-filter-write per `filterPlanReviewTag`'s contract. Because `--tags` replaces the whole list, the real tags were destroyed silently; the run reported `tagCleared: true` and looked clean.

Two defects to investigate, both in `.claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs`'s gate prompt builder (and its byte-identical copy in `.claude/workflows/plan-review.js`):

1. The gate prompt must make the agent read the target's current `tags` array, filter it, and write the exact remaining list — with the prompt carrying the read-back list, not a re-derived one. Consider having the driver compute the filtered list from the already-fetched JSON summary and pass the literal comma-separated value into the command template, so the mechanical agent has no room to invent tags.
2. Add a regression to `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` section 5 that seeds a real plan repo item with sibling tags plus `needs-plan-review`, runs the gate path, and asserts the post-gate tag list is exactly the siblings — the existing `filterPlanReviewTag` unit coverage passes while the end-to-end write is wrong, so a pure-helper test is not sufficient.

Separately (may be the same root cause or a second bug): the same run produced only TWO units for a 6-phase roadmap — one `kind: roadmap` unit and one `kind: phase` unit whose `ident` was the roadmap slug `workflow-token-reduction` rather than a phase stem, carrying findings that spanned phases 3, 4, 5 and 6 in a single verdict. The documented behavior is per-phase independent gating (one unit per phase, gated individually). The per-phase `parallel()` fan-out either did not happen or collapsed. Worth checking whether the phase-list fetch returned a shape the driver mis-parsed — the same mis-parse could explain the bogus tag values above.

coherence.concern: Defect 1's prescribed remedy is already implemented verbatim on `main`, so following the plan as written produces a no-op change while the clobber recurs.
coherence.location: .claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs:210-231 (buildTagWritePrompt) and :726 (`const remaining = filterPlanReviewTag(u.tags)`)
coherence.what_fails: The plan states "The gate prompt must make the agent read the target's current `tags` array, filter it, and write the exact remaining list" and proposes "having the driver compute the filtered list from the already-fetched JSON summary and pass the literal comma-separated value into the command template, so the mechanical agent has no room to invent tags." That is exactly the current code: the driver computes `filterPlanReviewTag(u.tags)` and passes it to `buildTagWritePrompt(kind, roadmap, ident, remainingTags)`, which builds `const tagsFlag = remainingTags.length === 0 ? '--tags ""' : '--tags "' + remainingTags.join(',') + '"'` and emits "Run exactly these two commands in the repo root:" with the fully-resolved `rdm <kind> update ... --tags "a,b"` literal. The prompt contains no read step and no filtering instruction for the agent to get wrong. `git log -L` on the function shows it has carried `remainingTags` since it was introduced (54448d8) — it was never an agent-side read-filter-write. An implementer following the plan opens the named builder, finds nothing to change, and either closes the task as already-fixed or makes a cosmetic edit; either way the observed clobber is untouched.
coherence.why: The plan asserts "Two defects to investigate, both in `.claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs`'s gate prompt builder" as settled fact, which directs the implementer's whole scope at a function that already satisfies the stated contract. This is a wrong-location/wrong-approach error, not a decision left to the implementer.
coherence.recommendation: Rewrite defect 1 to state the observed symptom without prescribing the already-implemented remedy, and re-scope it to where `u.tags` originates. Cite `buildTagWritePrompt`'s current signature explicitly as the baseline ("the driver already passes a literal filtered list; the bad values therefore entered via `u.tags`, not via agent-side filtering") so the implementer does not re-litigate a solved sub-problem.

coherence.concern: The plan's own evidence localizes the bug to the unvalidated fetch-result parse in `buildReviewUnits`, but the plan demotes that to an optional "worth checking" aside and defines no acceptance criterion covering it.
coherence.location: .claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs:490-539 (buildReviewUnits) and :620-631 (the `fetch:roadmap` mechanical agent call)
coherence.what_fails: `buildReviewUnits` trusts the mechanical fetch agent's returned JSON wholesale: `tags: Array.isArray(rm.tags) ? rm.tags : []` for the roadmap unit and, per phase, `ident: p.stem` / `tags: Array.isArray(p.tags) ? p.tags : []`. Both reported symptoms fall out of one bad `ROADMAP_TARGET` payload: `phases: [{ stem: 'workflow-token-reduction', tags: ['fetch','roadmap','workflow-token-reduction'], ... }]` yields exactly two units (one roadmap + one phase whose `ident` is the roadmap slug) and exactly the bogus tag list reported — the values are label-shaped, matching the fetch step's own identifiers rather than anything on the item. The only validation present is the fail-closed empty-body check; nothing validates `phases` length against `rdm phase list`, nothing rejects a `stem` equal to the roadmap slug, and nothing sanity-checks `tags`. The fetch agent is additionally pinned to the small tier (`model: _mechanicalModel`), which raises the odds of a mis-shaped return. Because the plan makes this a parenthetical ("Separately (may be the same root cause or a second bug)... Worth checking...") with no required fix and no acceptance criterion, an implementer can complete both numbered defects and still ship the clobber and the collapsed fan-out.
coherence.why: Scope, not detail: the plan directs mandatory work at a correct function and leaves the actual defect optional. Under the plan-stage contract this is a wrong-scope/wrong-approach error, and it is what would make the delivered change fail to fix the reported bug.
coherence.recommendation: Promote the fetch mis-parse to defect 1 and give it concrete acceptance criteria — e.g. `buildReviewUnits` fails closed (or the driver re-fetches) when the returned `phases` array is empty, when any `stem` equals the roadmap slug, or when the unit count disagrees with an independent `rdm phase list` count; and consider deriving the phase list deterministically rather than through an LLM fetch. State explicitly that the tag clobber and the unit collapse are one root cause unless evidence separates them.

coherence.concern: Defect 2's regression ("seeds a real plan repo item ... runs the gate path ... asserts the post-gate tag list") is not runnable in the named harness as written, and the gap it claims to close is already covered.
coherence.location: scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh (section 5 at :1130, section 5b-exec at :1374; existing assertion at :1528-1533)
coherence.what_fails: `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` contains zero occurrences of `target/debug/rdm` and zero `git init` calls — it is a static-grep plus Node-with-fakes harness, unlike `verify-worktree-review-loop.sh` / `verify-claude-code-web-loop.sh` which do seed real repos. More fundamentally, the gate's write is performed by an LLM agent (`_agent(buildTagWritePrompt(...), { label: 'gate:clear-tag:...' })`); in the harness that agent is a fake that records the prompt and never shells out, so "runs the gate path" against a real plan repo requires a bridging mechanism the plan does not specify. Separately, the assertion the plan asks for already exists in prompt form at :1528-1533: `assert.ok(tagCall.prompt.indexOf('--tags "depends-unlanded"') !== -1, 'the sibling tag is preserved in the write-back')`. So the new test as described would be either unimplementable or redundant, leaving the real uncovered surface — a mis-shaped fetch payload flowing into `u.tags`/`p.stem` — untested.
coherence.why: The two branches an implementer could take here (make the fake agent execute the emitted command against a seeded repo, versus assert on prompt text) differ in whether the regression can catch the reported bug at all, and the plan itself rules out the cheaper branch ("a pure-helper test is not sufficient"), so the ambiguity is outcome-changing rather than a free implementation choice.
coherence.recommendation: Specify the mechanism: either state that the harness's fake gate agent must execute the command string embedded in `buildTagWritePrompt`'s output against a temp `rdm`-seeded repo (adding real-binary seeding to this harness, as `verify-workflow-estimate.sh` already does), or re-target the regression at the actual gap — feed `runPlanReviewDriver` a deliberately mis-shaped `fetch:roadmap` payload (garbage `tags`, `stem` == roadmap slug, missing phases) and assert the driver fails closed and issues no `gate:clear-tag` call.

coherence.concern: The plan's evidence does not match the current plan-repo state, and the run artifact needed to reproduce is not recorded.
coherence.location: task body, paragraphs 2 and 4 ("a 6-phase roadmap", "it wrote `fetch, roadmap, workflow-token-reduction`")
coherence.what_fails: `rdm roadmap show workflow-token-reduction --project rdm --no-body` currently reports `Tags: cost, workflow, autonomy` and `Progress: 0/7 phases done` — the tags are the originals (so the clobber was evidently repaired out-of-band) and the roadmap has seven phases, not the six the plan cites. An implementer starting from the plan cannot observe the failure, and the only pointer to the raw evidence is the opaque run id `wf_e3402021-0af`; the actual `ROADMAP_TARGET` JSON the fetch agent returned — the single artifact that would confirm or refute the mis-parse hypothesis in the finding above — is not captured anywhere in the task.
coherence.why: Not goal- or scope-changing, so not blocking, but it removes the implementer's ability to confirm the root cause before fixing, which raises the risk they fix the wrong thing.
coherence.recommendation: Paste the offending fetch-step JSON (or the sidecar excerpt showing the `fetch:roadmap` return and the resulting unit list) into the task body, note that the roadmap's tags have since been restored so the failure is not reproducible from current state, and correct the phase count to seven (or say how many phases existed at run time).

architectural-fit.concern: architectural-fit
architectural-fit.location: .claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs:214-232 (buildTagWritePrompt) and :726-728 (gate call site); task body defect #1
architectural-fit.what_fails: The plan directs the fix at `buildTagWritePrompt`, but that builder already implements exactly what the plan proposes: the driver computes `const remaining = filterPlanReviewTag(u.tags)` (plan-review.mjs:726) and the builder interpolates the literal filtered list into the command template as `--tags "a,b"` (`const tagsFlag = remainingTags.length === 0 ? '--tags ""' : '--tags "' + remainingTags.join(',') + '"'`) — the mechanical agent is handed a fully-formed command with no room to invent tags. `git show 75e70af:.claude/workflows/plan-review.js` shows this signature and body verbatim since the workflow was created on 2026-07-24, i.e. before the 2026-07-25 run the task reports. Implementing the plan as written is a no-op edit while the real defect survives.
architectural-fit.why: The corrupted values can only have entered through `u.tags`, which `buildReviewUnits` copies from the mechanical LLM fetch agent's ROADMAP_TARGET/PLAN_TARGET payload (plan-review.mjs:501, :513, :532). That is the same payload `buildReviewUnits` fans out over to create per-phase units (`const phases = Array.isArray(rm.phases) ? rm.phases : []`, :505) — so a single under-delivered fetch response explains BOTH reported symptoms: `tags` populated with descriptor-ish junk AND one phase entry whose `stem` was the roadmap slug. The plan's own "separately, may be the same root cause" note points at this, then still scopes the fix to the gate builder. Architecturally the project's stated split is deterministic driver logic + strictly mechanical agents; here the driver treats an LLM transcription of `rdm roadmap show` + N `rdm phase show` outputs as trusted structured data with zero validation, and `buildRoadmapFetchPrompt` (:194-208) asks one agent — pinned to the small mechanical tier by f4e89d7, landed the day before the bad run — to transcribe six full phase bodies verbatim in one shot.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Re-scope the plan to the fetch boundary rather than the gate prompt builder. Concretely: (a) state that `buildTagWritePrompt` already carries the literal filtered list and needs no change, so the fix is not there; (b) add driver-side validation of the fetched payload before it is trusted — e.g. `buildReviewUnits` (or a new pure `validateFetchedRoadmap`) fails closed when `rm.phases.length` does not match the phase count the driver independently expects, or when a phase `stem` equals the roadmap slug, mirroring the existing fail-closed-on-empty-body precedent at :494/:522; (c) consider splitting `buildRoadmapFetchPrompt` into one cheap `roadmap show` fetch that yields the authoritative phase-stem list plus a `parallel()` per-stem `phase show` fetch, so no single small-model call has to transcribe six bodies and the fan-out width is driver-determined rather than agent-determined; and (d) since both symptoms share this root cause, fold the "separately" paragraph into the main defect instead of leaving it as an optional investigation.

architectural-fit.concern: architectural-fit
architectural-fit.location: scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh (section 5, line 1130 onward); task body defect #2
architectural-fit.what_fails: The plan asks section 5 to "seed a real plan repo item ... run the gate path, and assert the post-gate tag list is exactly the siblings". `verify-workflow-review.sh` contains zero `target/debug/rdm` invocations (grep count 0) and no `git init` / temp-repo seeding — it is entirely static greps plus Node driving the lib against injected fakes with no LLM calls, as CLAUDE.md documents. The gate's actual write is performed by a mechanical LLM agent executing the Bash command the prompt carries, so "running the gate path" end to end is not reachable in a hermetic harness. The plan supplies no mechanism, leaving the implementing agent to either invoke a model (violating the harness's stated hermetic/zero-LLM contract) or improvise.
architectural-fit.why: The stated constraint for this harness is hermetic, stdlib-only Node with an injected fake agent; the sibling real-binary seeding pattern lives in `scripts/verify-workflow-estimate.sh`, which gates on `[ -x "$RDM_BIN" ]` and is described separately in CLAUDE.md. Additionally, CLAUDE.md's hard rule forbids any direct access to `$RDM_ROOT`, so "a real plan repo item" must mean a temp git-backed repo seeded through the real binary — the plan does not say so. Note also that the assertion the plan wants already exists in a weaker form at verify-workflow-review.sh:1528 (`assert.ok(tagCall.prompt.indexOf('--tags "depends-unlanded"') !== -1)`), which is consistent with finding af-1: the untested boundary is fetch→`u.tags`, not the gate prompt.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Specify the mechanism explicitly: add a new hermetic-seed subsection modelled on `verify-workflow-estimate.sh` that (1) requires `$RDM_BIN` and seeds a TEMP git-backed plan repo via the real binary with `--tags needs-plan-review,cost,workflow`, (2) feeds that repo's actual `rdm roadmap show --format json` / `phase show --format json` output through `buildReviewUnits` + `runPlanReviewDriver` with a fake agent, (3) deterministically extracts the `rdm ... update ... --tags` line from the captured `gate:clear-tag:*` prompt and executes it with bash against the temp repo, then (4) asserts `rdm ... show --format json` reports exactly the siblings. That keeps zero LLM calls, stays off `$RDM_ROOT`, and — critically — exercises the fetch→units→tags path that the existing prompt-string assertion does not.

restraint.concern: Defect 1 pre-commits the fix to a specific mechanism and file location that the code already implements, over-specifying a decision the plan itself says still needs investigation
restraint.location: task/fix-plan-review-gate-tag-clobber — body, "Two defects to investigate, both in `.claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs`'s gate prompt builder" and item 1 ("Consider having the driver compute the filtered list from the already-fetched JSON summary and pass the literal comma-separated value into the command template")
restraint.what_fails: An implementing agent that follows item 1 as written opens `.claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs`'s gate prompt builder and finds the prescribed design is already in place, so it either makes a no-op edit or invents a redundant second mechanism, and the actual clobber is never fixed. Concretely: `runPlanReviewDriver` already calls `filterPlanReviewTag(u.tags)` on the already-fetched unit and passes the result into `buildTagWritePrompt(u.kind, u.roadmap, u.ident, remaining)` (lib/plan-review.mjs:726-731); `buildTagWritePrompt` (lib/plan-review.mjs:214-232, byte-identical at plan-review.js:1096) builds the literal `--tags "a,b"` string from that array and tells the agent "Run exactly these two commands". There is no read-back or re-derivation step in the gate for the agent to get wrong. The same is true of the requirement sentence above it ("the prompt carrying the read-back list, not a re-derived one") — that is already the shipped behavior.
restraint.why: The plan opens by framing this as "two defects to investigate", which is the right altitude for a bug whose root cause is not yet known. It then immediately narrows both to one function and names the mechanism to adopt. Because the observed symptoms — bogus tag values AND a 6-phase roadmap collapsing to one phase unit whose `ident` was the roadmap slug — are both fully explained by the mechanical fetch agent (`buildRoadmapFetchPrompt`, lib/plan-review.mjs:195-207) returning a malformed `ROADMAP_TARGET`, which `buildReviewUnits` then trusts verbatim (`tags: Array.isArray(rm.tags) ? rm.tags : []`, `ident: p.stem`, lines 501-516), the plan's own third paragraph already gestures at the right suspect ("Worth checking whether the phase-list fetch returned a shape the driver mis-parsed — the same mis-parse could explain the bogus tag values above") at exactly the restrained level this dimension wants. The over-specification in item 1 pulls against that paragraph and points the implementer away from it.
restraint.recommendation: Demote item 1 from a prescribed fix to a stated invariant plus evidence: keep "after the gate runs, the item's tag list must be exactly its pre-gate tags minus `needs-plan-review`" as the acceptance criterion, drop the `.mjs` gate-prompt-builder location claim and the "consider having the driver compute the filtered list" mechanism (noting instead that the driver already does this, so the corruption must enter upstream of the filter), and let the implementer locate the fault — most likely in the fetch step's contract or in `buildReviewUnits`'s unvalidated trust of the agent-returned shape. Keep item 2 as written; the end-to-end regression is the right level of specification and will hold whichever layer turns out to be at fault.

target:
phase project-agnostic-lane/phase-1-neutral-review-dimensions

## Context

~8 dimension blocks in `.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` hardcode rdm's own Rust
conventions into what is supposed to be a generic reviewer: `correctness` cites
rdm-core/anyhow error policy; `architecture` cites "logic in rdm-core with
cli/server as thin layers"; `api-docs` cites `#![warn(missing_docs)]` and rustdoc
`# Errors`/`# Panics`/`# Safety`; `changelog` asserts a CHANGELOG.md entry is
mandatory per CLAUDE.md.

SILENT breakage: a JS consumer repo gets a reviewer applying rustdoc rules. It
reaches two surfaces — `gen-workflow-review.sh` stamps the JS into three workflow
consumers, and `gen-skill-review.sh` renders the `//|` prose into
`skill-review-{cli,mcp}.md`, which SHIP.

**Design revised after plan review.** The original plan extended the emit-time
substitution pass to workflow content. That is unworkable and was found blocking:
`.claude/workflows/*.js` is both the template and the executed file, so a
`{principles}` placeholder would sit literally unsubstituted in the file rdm
itself runs; and any emit-time substitution breaks the byte-identity gates that
this roadmap otherwise leaves green.

Instead, conventions reach the reviewer the way `architectural-fit` ALREADY does
it: the dimension prose instructs the AGENT to read the project's principles file,
falling back to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md. Agents can read files; the JS does not need
to. No substitution pass, no placeholder, no gate change.

### Operator decision (2026-07-25) — the channel is prose only

Plan review raised two blocking unit-of-work findings against an earlier draft of
this phase, which added a persisted `principles_file` config key, threaded it to
the workflows as a runtime argument, and layered optional per-dimension convention
overrides on top. **Both are resolved by decision, not by implementation:**

- **The principles file lives at `docs/principles.md`, reached exactly the way the
  existing prose reviewers already reach it.** `architectural-fit`'s current
  `focus` string is the precedent and the whole mechanism: "Read the project's
  principles (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md if no principles note is configured)."
  Therefore: **no persisted `principles_file` key in `rdm-core`'s `Config`, no new
  runtime argument, and no per-dimension convention overrides.** The existing
  `rdm agent-config --principles-file` CLI flag (rdm-cli/src/cli.rs:160-162) is
  left exactly as it is. Per-dimension overrides are dropped from this roadmap
  outright — nothing downstream consumed them, and the roadmap's Problem section
  only ever asked for neutral prose plus a principles pointer.
- **This phase is therefore NOT split.** The unit-of-work objection was entirely
  about the config/runtime-arg bundle above; with that gone, what remains — rewrite
  the prose, verify `docs/principles.md` already states what the prose stops
  stating, mirror the template copies, regenerate both modes, re-fixture the pinned
  prompt baseline — is one atomic unit. It cannot be split further: the baseline
  re-fixture (step 6) is jointly unsatisfiable with the rewrite (step 1) unless
  both land in the same commit.

A welcome consequence: because no runtime argument is introduced, this phase no
longer front-runs any of phase 4's runtime-args plumbing, and it does not touch
the mechanism-2 byte-identical copies at all (see step 3).

### Scope boundary (what this phase does NOT touch)

This phase rewrites **dimension prose** — each dimension's `focus` string and its
`//|` spec lines in `lib/review.mjs` — and verifies the principles file already
covers what that prose stops stating. Two categories of rdm-specific text living
inside the same files are explicitly OUT of scope, and are excluded from this
phase's grep criteria:

- The `rdm-core/src/` path regex in `publicApiChanged`/`deriveSignals`
  (`lib/review.mjs`, stamped into all three consumers) — owned by phase 3
  ("Replace rdm repo-path regexes and Rust content patterns in deriveSignals").
- The stamped code comment referencing `rdm hook done-line` in `lib/review.mjs`,
  and the hand-written driver-region prose in `dispatch-phase.js` (the
  `rdm-core/src/ops/tag.rs` side-task example, and the `api-docs` round-2 comment)
  — hand-written regions owned by no step in this phase.

Also out of scope by the decision above: any change to `rdm-core/src/config.rs`,
any new workflow runtime argument, and the two mechanism-2 byte-identical lib↔js
copies (`lib/plan-review.mjs` ↔ `plan-review.js`'s `plan-review-driver` block;
`lib/dispatch-phase.mjs` ↔ `dispatch-phase.js`'s `dispatch-outcome` block). Those
blocks hold no dimension prose, and with no runtime arg to parse there is nothing
here that would turn their `diff` gates red.

## Steps

1. Rewrite each dimension's `focus` and `//|` prose to state generic INTENT — the
   error-handling conventions the project states, its layering contract, its
   documentation requirements — with no language or crate names, and to direct the
   agent to the project's principles file for specifics, falling back to
   CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md when none is configured. Follow `architectural-fit`'s
   existing `focus` string as the pattern to copy.
2. Point the rewritten prose at the EXISTING `docs/principles.md` — do NOT author a
   second principles document. Verify each convention removed in step 1 is already
   stated there: layering (§1 "Core Is the Source of Truth", §2 "Interaction Layers
   Are Thin Adapters"), error handling (§5 "Matchable Error Enums in Core" — hand-
   written enums, no `anyhow` in core, consumers add context), and doc sections
   (§8 "Public API Is Fully Documented" — `#![warn(missing_docs)]`,
   `# Errors`/`# Panics`/`# Safety`). The changelog rule is ALREADY there too —
   §13 "Conventional Commits and Changelogs" states "Every user-facing change gets
   a changelog entry" plus the Keep a Changelog `[Unreleased]`/category rules — so
   verify §13 rather than restating it; an earlier draft of this step wrongly
   called it a gap living only in CLAUDE.md. The narrower genuine delta versus
   CLAUDE.md is the SAME-COMMIT strictness ("MUST include a corresponding
   CHANGELOG.md update in the same commit. Do not defer changelog entries to a
   later commit or batch them up"). Add only that clause to §13, and only if §13
   still lacks it — do not duplicate the rule itself.
3. Mirror every workflow `.js` edit into `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js`
   so the byte-identity gates stay green. The mechanism-2 byte-identical lib↔js
   copies are deliberately NOT in scope — see the Scope boundary.
4. Re-run `gen-workflow-review.sh` and `gen-skill-review.sh` in BOTH modes.
5. Re-fixture the PINNED prompt baseline in the SAME commit as the step-1 rewrite.
   `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` asserts code-mode finder prompts are
   BYTE-EXACT against the hardcoded `CODE_PROMPT_BASELINE` map
   (verify-workflow-review.sh:604-611), which embeds the exact strings step 1
   deletes (`correctness`'s "In rdm-core, errors must be hand-written matchable
   enums (no anyhow / type erasure)…"; `architecture`'s "Does logic live in
   rdm-core with cli/server as thin layers?…"). Without this step the final AC
   ("verify-workflow-review.sh passes in both modes") and step 1 are jointly
   unsatisfiable. Update `CODE_PROMPT_BASELINE` — and any plan-mode prompt
   assertions embedding rewritten prose — to the new neutral `focus` strings,
   keeping the byte-exact form so the baseline's prompt-prose leak-detection
   purpose survives rather than being loosened to a substring match.
6. Update the two HAND-MAINTAINED dogfood skill copies, which `gen-skill-review.sh`
   does NOT write (its consumer list is only
   `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-{review,plan-review}-{cli,mcp}.md`, script lines
   73-75) even though each carries an `rdm:review-spec` region whose header claims
   generator ownership: `.claude/skills/rdm-review/SKILL.md` (region at :98, still
   containing the api-docs prose this phase deletes — "the diff changes a public

planDoc:
## Context

~8 dimension blocks in `.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` hardcode rdm's own Rust
conventions into what is supposed to be a generic reviewer: `correctness` cites
rdm-core/anyhow error policy; `architecture` cites "logic in rdm-core with
cli/server as thin layers"; `api-docs` cites `#![warn(missing_docs)]` and rustdoc
`# Errors`/`# Panics`/`# Safety`; `changelog` asserts a CHANGELOG.md entry is
mandatory per CLAUDE.md.

SILENT breakage: a JS consumer repo gets a reviewer applying rustdoc rules. It
reaches two surfaces — `gen-workflow-review.sh` stamps the JS into three workflow
consumers, and `gen-skill-review.sh` renders the `//|` prose into
`skill-review-{cli,mcp}.md`, which SHIP.

**Design revised after plan review.** The original plan extended the emit-time
substitution pass to workflow content. That is unworkable and was found blocking:
`.claude/workflows/*.js` is both the template and the executed file, so a
`{principles}` placeholder would sit literally unsubstituted in the file rdm
itself runs; and any emit-time substitution breaks the byte-identity gates that
this roadmap otherwise leaves green.

Instead, conventions reach the reviewer the way `architectural-fit` ALREADY does
it: the dimension prose instructs the AGENT to read the project's principles file,
falling back to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md. Agents can read files; the JS does not need
to. No substitution pass, no placeholder, no gate change.

### Operator decision (2026-07-25) — the channel is prose only

Plan review raised two blocking unit-of-work findings against an earlier draft of
this phase, which added a persisted `principles_file` config key, threaded it to
the workflows as a runtime argument, and layered optional per-dimension convention
overrides on top. **Both are resolved by decision, not by implementation:**

- **The principles file lives at `docs/principles.md`, reached exactly the way the
  existing prose reviewers already reach it.** `architectural-fit`'s current
  `focus` string is the precedent and the whole mechanism: "Read the project's
  principles (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md if no principles note is configured)."
  Therefore: **no persisted `principles_file` key in `rdm-core`'s `Config`, no new
  runtime argument, and no per-dimension convention overrides.** The existing
  `rdm agent-config --principles-file` CLI flag (rdm-cli/src/cli.rs:160-162) is
  left exactly as it is. Per-dimension overrides are dropped from this roadmap
  outright — nothing downstream consumed them, and the roadmap's Problem section
  only ever asked for neutral prose plus a principles pointer.
- **This phase is therefore NOT split.** The unit-of-work objection was entirely
  about the config/runtime-arg bundle above; with that gone, what remains — rewrite
  the prose, verify `docs/principles.md` already states what the prose stops
  stating, mirror the template copies, regenerate both modes, re-fixture the pinned
  prompt baseline — is one atomic unit. It cannot be split further: the baseline
  re-fixture (step 6) is jointly unsatisfiable with the rewrite (step 1) unless
  both land in the same commit.

A welcome consequence: because no runtime argument is introduced, this phase no
longer front-runs any of phase 4's runtime-args plumbing, and it does not touch
the mechanism-2 byte-identical copies at all (see step 3).

### Scope boundary (what this phase does NOT touch)

This phase rewrites **dimension prose** — each dimension's `focus` string and its
`//|` spec lines in `lib/review.mjs` — and verifies the principles file already
covers what that prose stops stating. Two categories of rdm-specific text living
inside the same files are explicitly OUT of scope, and are excluded from this
phase's grep criteria:

- The `rdm-core/src/` path regex in `publicApiChanged`/`deriveSignals`
  (`lib/review.mjs`, stamped into all three consumers) — owned by phase 3
  ("Replace rdm repo-path regexes and Rust content patterns in deriveSignals").
- The stamped code comment referencing `rdm hook done-line` in `lib/review.mjs`,
  and the hand-written driver-region prose in `dispatch-phase.js` (the
  `rdm-core/src/ops/tag.rs` side-task example, and the `api-docs` round-2 comment)
  — hand-written regions owned by no step in this phase.

Also out of scope by the decision above: any change to `rdm-core/src/config.rs`,
any new workflow runtime argument, and the two mechanism-2 byte-identical lib↔js
copies (`lib/plan-review.mjs` ↔ `plan-review.js`'s `plan-review-driver` block;
`lib/dispatch-phase.mjs` ↔ `dispatch-phase.js`'s `dispatch-outcome` block). Those
blocks hold no dimension prose, and with no runtime arg to parse there is nothing
here that would turn their `diff` gates red.

## Steps

1. Rewrite each dimension's `focus` and `//|` prose to state generic INTENT — the
   error-handling conventions the project states, its layering contract, its
   documentation requirements — with no language or crate names, and to direct the
   agent to the project's principles file for specifics, falling back to
   CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md when none is configured. Follow `architectural-fit`'s
   existing `focus` string as the pattern to copy.
2. Point the rewritten prose at the EXISTING `docs/principles.md` — do NOT author a
   second principles document. Verify each convention removed in step 1 is already
   stated there: layering (§1 "Core Is the Source of Truth", §2 "Interaction Layers
   Are Thin Adapters"), error handling (§5 "Matchable Error Enums in Core" — hand-
   written enums, no `anyhow` in core, consumers add context), and doc sections
   (§8 "Public API Is Fully Documented" — `#![warn(missing_docs)]`,
   `# Errors`/`# Panics`/`# Safety`). The changelog rule is ALREADY there too —
   §13 "Conventional Commits and Changelogs" states "Every user-facing change gets
   a changelog entry" plus the Keep a Changelog `[Unreleased]`/category rules — so
   verify §13 rather than restating it; an earlier draft of this step wrongly
   called it a gap living only in CLAUDE.md. The narrower genuine delta versus
   CLAUDE.md is the SAME-COMMIT strictness ("MUST include a corresponding
   CHANGELOG.md update in the same commit. Do not defer changelog entries to a
   later commit or batch them up"). Add only that clause to §13, and only if §13
   still lacks it — do not duplicate the rule itself.
3. Mirror every workflow `.js` edit into `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js`
   so the byte-identity gates stay green. The mechanism-2 byte-identical lib↔js
   copies are deliberately NOT in scope — see the Scope boundary.
4. Re-run `gen-workflow-review.sh` and `gen-skill-review.sh` in BOTH modes.
5. Re-fixture the PINNED prompt baseline in the SAME commit as the step-1 rewrite.
   `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` asserts code-mode finder prompts are
   BYTE-EXACT against the hardcoded `CODE_PROMPT_BASELINE` map
   (verify-workflow-review.sh:604-611), which embeds the exact strings step 1
   deletes (`correctness`'s "In rdm-core, errors must be hand-written matchable
   enums (no anyhow / type erasure)…"; `architecture`'s "Does logic live in
   rdm-core with cli/server as thin layers?…"). Without this step the final AC
   ("verify-workflow-review.sh passes in both modes") and step 1 are jointly
   unsatisfiable. Update `CODE_PROMPT_BASELINE` — and any plan-mode prompt
   assertions embedding rewritten prose — to the new neutral `focus` strings,
   keeping the byte-exact form so the baseline's prompt-prose leak-detection
   purpose survives rather than being loosened to a substring match.
6. Update the two HAND-MAINTAINED dogfood skill copies, which `gen-skill-review.sh`
   does NOT write (its consumer list is only
   `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-{review,plan-review}-{cli,mcp}.md`, script lines
   73-75) even though each carries an `rdm:review-spec` region whose header claims
   generator ownership: `.claude/skills/rdm-review/SKILL.md` (region at :98, still
   containing the api-docs prose this phase deletes — "the diff changes a public
   `rdm-core` item", `#![warn(missing_docs)]`, `# Errors`/`# Panics`/`# Safety` at
   :139-141) and `.claude/skills/rdm-plan-review/SKILL.md` (region at :48).
   Regenerate them the way they are normally produced (`./target/debug/rdm
   agent-config claude --skills --out .claude/skills`, or extend the generator's
   consumer list) so rdm's own interactive reviewer stops applying the
   language-specific rules the shipped surface no longer states.
7. Update `docs/workflow-schemas.md`'s `buildReviewPipeline(mode, deps?)` /
   dimension-table / `context` sections (:241-296) to match the rewritten dimension
   prose — CLAUDE.md names that document the canonical home of these contracts, so
   leaving it describing the old dimension semantics is a stated-convention
   violation. Note this phase introduces no new pipeline input, so the `context`
   contract itself is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

      and (b) the dimension prose regions ONLY — the `DIMENSIONS` object and `//|`

      The `deriveSignals`/`publicApiChanged` `rdm-core/src/` pattern (phase 3) and
      `dispatch-phase.js`'s hand-written driver-region prose are excluded per the
      Scope boundary above. Whole-file zero-grep is a ROADMAP-level criterion,

- [ ] No `{principles}` or other placeholder token is introduced into any

- [ ] The byte-identity gates remain GREEN — this phase changes no emission
      behavior
- [ ] **NEGATIVE criterion (per the operator decision above):** `rdm-core/src/config.rs`

- [ ] `docs/principles.md` covers every convention removed in step 1 — layering
      (§1/§2), error handling (§5), doc sections (§8), and the changelog rule (§13)

      the same-commit clause to §13: §13 states that a user-facing change's

      NO second principles document is created, and no already-present rule is

# Phase 2: Rebuild the security dimension on a threat-model taxonomy; delete the Rust greps

## Context

The `security` dimension is currently gated by two Rust-only constructs in
`lib/review.mjs` — cite them by symbol, not line number:

- `SECURITY_DIFF_PATTERNS` (currently :610-617) = `std::process`,
  `Command::new`, `std::fs::`, `env::var`, `from_utf8_unchecked`,
  `set_permissions`
- the `hasUnsafe` grep (currently :664) = `/(^|\n)\+.*\bunsafe\b/`

Do **not** navigate by the line numbers alone — the nearby `CODE_EXTENSIONS`
and `TEST_PATH_PATTERNS` lists are explicitly protected by phase 3 and must not
be touched here.

In a JS repo, `child_process.exec` never trips `securitySurface` and `hasUnsafe`
is meaningless — the dimension silently never fires. These greps are also the
wrong shape of check independent of language: they LLM-encode what a static
linter (clippy) already does, rather than asking a security question.

Claude Code's shipped security skill is the model
(`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/claude-security/agents/scan-researcher.md`
— read it before starting). Its framing: "a finding is a claim that an attacker
can do something they should not be able to do, and you must be able to point at
the code that lets them — not lint, not style, not 'consider using a safer API'."

Decisive argument for dropping the greps: that skill's language-neutral `memory`
category already covers `unsafe-ffi`, `use-after-free`, and `out-of-bounds-*`
generically. The six diff patterns plus the `unsafe` grep buy no coverage a
generic taxonomy lacks.

### Two projections, two audiences (read before step 4)

`lib/review.mjs` has TWO independent projections, and they reach disjoint
audiences. Getting this wrong is the single most likely way to ship this phase
"green but useless":

- **Runtime.** `scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh` stamps the JS block into the
  three workflow consumers. What an actual finder agent receives is assembled by
  `findPrompt(mode, dim, context)` (:285-305) from fixed strings plus `dim.focus`
  plus the `PLAN_SEVERITY_CALIBRATION` const. This is the surface the autonomous
  lane (`dispatch-phase.js`, `autopilot.js`, `plan-review.js`,
  `review-refute-fix.js`) actually executes.
- **Documentation.** `scripts/gen-skill-review.sh` renders `//|` spec prose into
  the shipped skill templates. Its `extract_region` awk only ever reads lines
  matching `/^[[:space:]]*\/\/\|/`. `//|` lines are **inert comments at
  runtime** — `findPrompt` never reads them.

Consequence: prose-only placement of the injection hygiene would reach every
shipped markdown template and ZERO executing reviewers; const-only placement
would reach every executing reviewer and no template. Step 4 therefore requires
**both**, and the acceptance criteria assert them separately.

### Surface inventory (read before step 7)

`scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh` stamps only **three** files, and
`scripts/gen-skill-review.sh` renders only the **shipped** skill templates.
Neither generator touches the shipped workflow copies under
`rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/`, the hand-maintained dogfood skill copies,
the harness, the schema doc, or the hand-authored (outside-the-markers) prose in
the shipped skill templates. The full set of surfaces this phase must leave
consistent is:

## Steps

   `deriveSignals` return object (:664) **together** — never one without the

   Only security-specific framing stays inside the `security` dimension, which is

6. Retire the now-obsolete `hasUnsafe` assertions in

      command-injection finding is out of scope — the harness agent is a spy.

      phase 3 — which now OWNS it by operator decision, with its own acceptance

      diff-pattern trigger
- [ ] `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh`,
      `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh`, and
      `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` all pass
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] — this phase rewrites the shipped
      `skill-review-{cli,mcp}.md` / `skill-plan-review-{cli,mcp}.md` templates
      that `rdm agent-config` emits, which is user-facing, and the `changelog`
      dimension this pipeline runs on itself treats a missing entry as `blocking`

`.claude/workflows/*.js` and `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js` are

(`generate_workflows_are_byte_identical_to_source`, agent_config.rs:1249; section 3

## Steps

1. Read the reference agent and extract the reusable pieces: the category
   vocabulary (injection / authorization / memory / crypto / exposure), the
   impact-based HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW severity ladder, and the `(file, line, category)`
   dedupe key.
2. Rewrite the `security` dimension `focus` and `//|code|` prose on the
   threat-model framing — an attacker capability plus the code that grants it —
   with the category vocabulary replacing the pattern lists. Explicitly exclude
   lint and style findings.
3. Delete `SECURITY_DIFF_PATTERNS` and the `hasUnsafe` grep, and remove
   `hasUnsafe` from the `security` dimension's `when` predicate (:192, leaving
   `(s) => !!s.securitySurface`). **`hasUnsafe` leaves the signal contract
   entirely:** remove it from the `SIGNAL_KEYS` array (:549-557) *and* from the
   `deriveSignals` return object (:664) **together** — never one without the
   other. The fully-populated-signals invariant documented at :545-547 (and
   asserted by the `typeof d1[key] === 'boolean'` loop in the harness) is
   load-bearing: a key listed in `SIGNAL_KEYS` but not set by `deriveSignals`
   makes a dimension drop out on a MISSING key rather than a real negative. Then
   update `docs/workflow-schemas.md`'s `deriveSignals` section (:296-303) so its
   `SIGNAL_KEYS` enumeration and any `unsafe` trigger prose match the
   post-change code. **Scope boundary:** after this phase `securitySurface` triggers on
   `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` alone — a defined, documented, path-based behavior,
   not an undefined one. Content-based triggering for non-Rust sinks that sit in
   paths matching no security path pattern is a *generic* signal problem and is
   implemented by **phase 3**, not here. This phase's deliverable is the written
   decision (recorded in the dimension prose and the commit message) plus the
   deletion; phase 3 step 4 folds that decision in.

   **The phase-3 decision is now MADE (operator, 2026-07-25): content triggering,
   and `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` is REMOVED there.** So the path-only state this
   phase lands is explicitly INTERIM, not the destination — a one-phase waypoint,
   which is why it is safe to land here with the path-based acceptance criteria
   below. Phase 3 step 4 supersedes them and re-fixtures the assertions; do not
   treat the path-based trigger as a durable contract, and do not add new
   `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` entries here.
4. Adopt "the repository is not talking to you" prompt-injection hygiene. The
   stated threat is fleet-wide — every reviewer reads plan documents and diffs,
   which are untrusted input — so the hygiene text goes in **BOTH** placements.
   These are not alternatives: per "Two projections, two audiences" above, each
   one alone reaches only half the audience.
   - **Runtime:** add a shared const alongside `PLAN_SEVERITY_CALIBRATION` (e.g.
     `INJECTION_HYGIENE`) and have `findPrompt` push it **unconditionally** —
     for both `code` and `plan` mode and for every dimension, not inside the
     `if (mode === 'plan')` branch. This is what executing finder agents receive,
     and `gen-workflow-review.sh` stamps it into all three workflow consumers.
   - **Documentation:** add the same text as shared, **untagged** `//|` prose in
     the finder-prompt region, so `gen-skill-review.sh` renders it into both
     modes' templates.
   Only security-specific framing stays inside the `security` dimension, which is
   `code`-mode-only and conditionally selected. This makes
   `gen-skill-review.sh --mode plan` a required regeneration. Add the runtime
   assertion described in the acceptance criteria to the existing Node section of
   `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` — the `context.target threaded into finder
   prompts` checks (:504, :589) are the pattern to copy.
5. Reconcile the severity ladder with the existing `blocking | concern |
   suggestion` contract — map, do not duplicate.
6. Retire the now-obsolete `hasUnsafe` assertions in
   `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh`. These are **expected work for this
   phase**, not a regression to patch around — the signal they pin no longer
   exists. Cite by symbol, verify by grep (`grep -n hasUnsafe
   scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh`), and remove exactly:
   - the `TRIGGER_MATRIX` row `['hasUnsafe', 'security']` (:807) — it asserts
     `selectDimensions('code', { hasUnsafe: true })` includes `security`, which is
     false once step 3 drops it from the `when` predicate;
   - `assert.equal(d1.hasUnsafe, false, …)` (:854) and the "an added `unsafe` line
     trips hasUnsafe" assertion (:856-858) — both read `undefined` under
     `assert/strict` after the deletion;
   - the `hasUnsafe: false` key in the no-input whole-object
     `assert.deepEqual(deriveSignals(), { … })` (:864-874).

   Also reword the now-misleading message on
   `assert.equal(d1.securitySurface, true, 'std::process in the diff trips
   securitySurface')` (:853): that assertion still passes, but only via the
   fixture's `hook.rs` **path** pattern, not the deleted diff pattern. The new

7. Propagate to every surface in the inventory above: run

## Acceptance Criteria

## Context

`deriveSignals` decides which conditional dimensions run. Two of its inputs are
hardcoded to rdm's own repo layout. **Navigate by SYMBOL, not by line number** —
phase 2 deletes `SECURITY_DIFF_PATTERNS` and the `hasUnsafe` content pattern from
this same source ahead of this phase, so every line number below will have
drifted; verify each site by grep. The source of truth is
`.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` (`USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS` ≈:618-623,
`publicApiChanged` ≈:658-659, `userFacing` ≈:660, the `changelog` dimension's
`when` ≈:165); `review-refute-fix.js` and `dispatch-phase.js` hold
generator-stamped copies at DIFFERENT line numbers — do not edit those copies.

- `USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS = [/^rdm-cli\//, /^rdm-server\//,
  /(^|[/_.-])mcp([/_.-]|$)/, /(^|[/_.-])config([/_.-]|$)/]` — quote the list in
  FULL; the last two patterns matter (see below)
- `publicApiChanged: lower.some((p) => p.indexOf('rdm-core/src/') === 0) &&
  (diffText === null || /(^|\n)\+.*\bpub\b/.test(diffText))` — quote this
  expression in FULL too. It has TWO rdm-specific halves, and the second is easy
  to miss: a path prefix AND a **Rust-keyword content clause** (`\bpub\b`).

**The two signals fail differently — fix both.**

- `publicApiChanged` is hard-gated on the `rdm-core/src/` prefix, so in any other
  repo it is permanently, confidently `false` and the `api-docs` dimension NEVER
  FIRES. The review completes, reports clean, and has silently skipped a
  dimension.
- **The `\bpub\b` conjunct is the second half of that same defect, and replacing
  the path prefix alone does not fix it.** In a TypeScript repo, a diff of
  `+export function foo()` under a declared public-API path still yields
  `\bpub\b` → false → `publicApiChanged` false → `api-docs` still never fires.
  Note the clause is short-circuited by `diffText === null`, so a test that
  passes only `changedFiles` reads `true` and does NOT catch this; both real
  drivers always supply a non-null `diffText` off a populated diff agent result
  (`review-refute-fix.js:986-990`, `dispatch-phase.js:1731-1735`), so the bug is
  invisible to any fixture that omits `diffText`.
- `userFacing` does NOT go silent: the `mcp` and `config` patterns are
  repo-agnostic. In any JS/TS repo a diff touching `next.config.js`,
  `vite.config.ts`, or `src/config/index.ts` sets `userFacing: true` and
  the `changelog` dimension (`when: (s) => !!s.userFacing`) fires on a path
  spelling coincidence, while a genuinely user-facing change under a
  differently-named path is skipped. The defect here is a confident, incidentally
  **true** signal — the opposite polarity from `publicApiChanged`, and it is NOT
  fixed by only eliminating confident-false.

This is the most dangerous category in the roadmap: it degrades rather than fails.

`CODE_EXTENSIONS` is already multi-language and correct — leave it.
`TEST_PATH_PATTERNS` is convention-based rather than rdm-specific; audit it but
expect it to survive largely intact. `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` does **not** survive
— see step 4 and the operator decision: `securitySurface` moves to content
triggering and the path list is removed. (An earlier draft of this line expected it
to survive intact; that expectation is superseded.)

Note the existing three-way fail-open contract in `selectDimensions` is
load-bearing and carefully reasoned (`signals == null` → ALL dimensions; `{}` →
always-on only). Do not weaken it. The bug here is the opposite failure: signals
were computed and came back confidently, wrongly, false.

### Blast radius: three harnesses and a third copy the generators do not reach

Two things about this repo's layout make the change wider than "edit
`lib/review.mjs` and re-run one generator":

1. **`deriveSignals`' rdm-path behavior is pinned by assertions in THREE
   harnesses**, and CLAUDE.md's CI expectation runs every one of them
   (`for f in scripts/verify-*.sh; do bash "$f"; done`):

     `rdm-core/src` trips `publicApiChanged`" / "an rdm-cli path trips

## Operator decision (2026-07-25) — content, not declared paths

An earlier draft of this phase routed project-declared public-API and user-facing
paths "through the phase 1 config channel", and left step 4 (`securitySurface`
triggering) as an unbounded, AC-free handoff from phase 2. Plan review found the
latter blocking. **Both are resolved by decision:**

- **Every signal derives from diff CONTENT, not from declared or conventional
  paths.** There is no generic way to specify paths that works across repos — a
  path list is either repo-specific (the `rdm-core/src/` defect this phase exists
  to remove) or fires on spelling coincidence (the `mcp`/`config` defect below).
  Phase 1's config channel does not exist (that decision dropped the persisted
  config key entirely), so there is nothing to route through and nothing to
  declare.
- **When content cannot decide, the signal is genuinely ABSENT, not `false`** —
  engaging `selectDimensions`' existing `signals == null` fail-open path — scoped
  so that a docs-only diff still resolves to a legitimate `false` (step 3).
- **`securitySurface` triggers on content too, and `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` is
  removed** (step 4). This closes phase 2's deferred handoff with a real
  deliverable and a real acceptance criterion.

Consequence worth noting: because content derivation reads `diffText` and
`changedFiles`, which every caller ALREADY supplies, this phase introduces **no
new `deriveSignals` input**. That removes the entire arg-threading surface the
earlier draft had to cover — see step 7.

## Steps

1. Audit every pattern list in `deriveSignals` and classify each as
   repo-specific, convention-based, or language-specific.
2. Replace the repo-specific ones with **language-neutral CONTENT derivation** —
   see the operator decision above. `publicApiChanged` has two rdm-specific
   halves and both go: delete the `rdm-core/src/` path prefix outright (do not
   generalize it into a declared-path list), and replace the Rust-only `\bpub\b`
   conjunct with a language-neutral export/visibility notion derived from the
   diff content itself (added lines introducing an exported/public symbol across
   the languages `CODE_EXTENSIONS` already covers). Do NOT leave `\bpub\b` in
   place behind any generalized path check — the signal would stay confidently
   false in every non-Rust repo (see Context). The same rule applies to
   `userFacing`: derive it from content, not from path spelling.
3. Apply the fail-open policy for what content cannot decide: a signal that
   cannot be computed must NOT resolve to a confident `false`. Make it

## Context

`deriveSignals` decides which conditional dimensions run. Two of its inputs are
hardcoded to rdm's own repo layout. **Navigate by SYMBOL, not by line number** —
phase 2 deletes `SECURITY_DIFF_PATTERNS` and the `hasUnsafe` content pattern from
this same source ahead of this phase, so every line number below will have
drifted; verify each site by grep. The source of truth is
`.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` (`USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS` ≈:618-623,
`publicApiChanged` ≈:658-659, `userFacing` ≈:660, the `changelog` dimension's
`when` ≈:165); `review-refute-fix.js` and `dispatch-phase.js` hold
generator-stamped copies at DIFFERENT line numbers — do not edit those copies.

- `USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS = [/^rdm-cli\//, /^rdm-server\//,
  /(^|[/_.-])mcp([/_.-]|$)/, /(^|[/_.-])config([/_.-]|$)/]` — quote the list in
  FULL; the last two patterns matter (see below)
- `publicApiChanged: lower.some((p) => p.indexOf('rdm-core/src/') === 0) &&
  (diffText === null || /(^|\n)\+.*\bpub\b/.test(diffText))` — quote this
  expression in FULL too. It has TWO rdm-specific halves, and the second is easy
  to miss: a path prefix AND a **Rust-keyword content clause** (`\bpub\b`).

**The two signals fail differently — fix both.**

- `publicApiChanged` is hard-gated on the `rdm-core/src/` prefix, so in any other
  repo it is permanently, confidently `false` and the `api-docs` dimension NEVER
  FIRES. The review completes, reports clean, and has silently skipped a
  dimension.
- **The `\bpub\b` conjunct is the second half of that same defect, and replacing
  the path prefix alone does not fix it.** In a TypeScript repo, a diff of
  `+export function foo()` under a declared public-API path still yields
  `\bpub\b` → false → `publicApiChanged` false → `api-docs` still never fires.
  Note the clause is short-circuited by `diffText === null`, so a test that
  passes only `changedFiles` reads `true` and does NOT catch this; both real
  drivers always supply a non-null `diffText` off a populated diff agent result
  (`review-refute-fix.js:986-990`, `dispatch-phase.js:1731-1735`), so the bug is
  invisible to any fixture that omits `diffText`.
- `userFacing` does NOT go silent: the `mcp` and `config` patterns are
  repo-agnostic. In any JS/TS repo a diff touching `next.config.js`,
  `vite.config.ts`, or `src/config/index.ts` sets `userFacing: true` and
  the `changelog` dimension (`when: (s) => !!s.userFacing`) fires on a path
  spelling coincidence, while a genuinely user-facing change under a
  differently-named path is skipped. The defect here is a confident, incidentally
  **true** signal — the opposite polarity from `publicApiChanged`, and it is NOT
  fixed by only eliminating confident-false.

This is the most dangerous category in the roadmap: it degrades rather than fails.

`CODE_EXTENSIONS` is already multi-language and correct — leave it.
`TEST_PATH_PATTERNS` is convention-based rather than rdm-specific; audit it but
expect it to survive largely intact. `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` does **not** survive
— see step 4 and the operator decision: `securitySurface` moves to content
triggering and the path list is removed. (An earlier draft of this line expected it
to survive intact; that expectation is superseded.)

Note the existing three-way fail-open contract in `selectDimensions` is
load-bearing and carefully reasoned (`signals == null` → ALL dimensions; `{}` →
always-on only). Do not weaken it. The bug here is the opposite failure: signals
were computed and came back confidently, wrongly, false.

### Blast radius: three harnesses and a third copy the generators do not reach

Two things about this repo's layout make the change wider than "edit
`lib/review.mjs` and re-run one generator":

1. **`deriveSignals`' rdm-path behavior is pinned by assertions in THREE
   harnesses**, and CLAUDE.md's CI expectation runs every one of them
   (`for f in scripts/verify-*.sh; do bash "$f"; done`):
   - `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh:849-850` asserts "a `+pub` line under
     `rdm-core/src` trips `publicApiChanged`" / "an rdm-cli path trips
     `userFacing`"; **:866-874 is a `deepEqual` pinning a no-input
     `deriveSignals()` to `publicApiChanged: false, userFacing: false`** — which
     is precisely the confident-false this phase forbids. That assertion is NOT
     an invariant to preserve; it must be rewritten to encode the new behavior.
   - `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh:781-783` asserts
     `deriveSignals({changedFiles:['rdm-core/src/ops/task.rs'], diffText:'+pub fn foo() {}'}).publicApiChanged === true`,
     and :813-814 asserts a docs-only round leaves it `false`.
   - `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh:288/304` seed
     `rdm-core/src/foo.rs` and `rdm-cli/src/x.rs` diffs; :338 seeds a
     deliberately non-triggering docs-only case.

   Removing the rdm literals necessarily breaks the rdm-crate-path fixtures in
   all three. Re-fixturing them onto the same synthetic non-rdm project the
   acceptance criteria already require is **expected work for this phase**, not a
   regression to avoid.

   **The three surviving docs-only "non-triggering" assertions are a separate
   case and must NOT be swept up in that re-fixturing** —
   `verify-workflow-review.sh:797-801` (derive from `['docs/workflow-schemas.md']`
   with no declared config, then assert `selectDimensions('code', docsSignals)` is
   exactly `['ac','correctness']`), `verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh:340-344`
   (`['docs/readme.md']` → always-on only), and
   `verify-workflow-dispatch.sh:812-814` (round 1 docs-only leaves
   `publicApiChanged` off, which is the discriminator for the re-derivation test).
   They are governed by step 3's undeterminable-signal policy, not by the removed
   rdm literals, and they collide head-on with the "no configuration present →
   still select the dimension" criterion unless that policy is scoped as step 3
   specifies. See step 3 and step 5.

2. **`rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js` are hand-maintained `include_str!`
   copies that NO generator writes.** `scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh` rewrites
   only `.claude/workflows/{review-refute-fix,dispatch-phase,plan-review}.js`.
   The shipped copies under `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` are byte-identity
   gated by `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` (section 3,
   `check_workflows_byte_identical`, :160-168) and
   `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh:79`. Regenerating without syncing
   them leaves `verify-workflow-review.sh` green while turning those two red on
   `main`. The roadmap's Scope note ("edit the LIB and re-run the generator") is
   an incomplete description of the architecture — there is a third copy.

## Operator decision (2026-07-25) — content, not declared paths

An earlier draft of this phase routed project-declared public-API and user-facing
paths "through the phase 1 config channel", and left step 4 (`securitySurface`
triggering) as an unbounded, AC-free handoff from phase 2. Plan review found the
latter blocking. **Both are resolved by decision:**

- **Every signal derives from diff CONTENT, not from declared or conventional
  paths.** There is no generic way to specify paths that works across repos — a
  path list is either repo-specific (the `rdm-core/src/` defect this phase exists
  to remove) or fires on spelling coincidence (the `mcp`/`config` defect below).
  Phase 1's config channel does not exist (that decision dropped the persisted
  config key entirely), so there is nothing to route through and nothing to
  declare.
- **When content cannot decide, the signal is genuinely ABSENT, not `false`** —
  engaging `selectDimensions`' existing `signals == null` fail-open path — scoped
  so that a docs-only diff still resolves to a legitimate `false` (step 3).
- **`securitySurface` triggers on content too, and `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` is
  removed** (step 4). This closes phase 2's deferred handoff with a real
  deliverable and a real acceptance criterion.

Consequence worth noting: because content derivation reads `diffText` and
`changedFiles`, which every caller ALREADY supplies, this phase introduces **no
new `deriveSignals` input**. That removes the entire arg-threading surface the
earlier draft had to cover — see step 7.

## Steps

1. Audit every pattern list in `deriveSignals` and classify each as
   repo-specific, convention-based, or language-specific.
2. Replace the repo-specific ones with **language-neutral CONTENT derivation** —
   see the operator decision above. `publicApiChanged` has two rdm-specific
   halves and both go: delete the `rdm-core/src/` path prefix outright (do not
   generalize it into a declared-path list), and replace the Rust-only `\bpub\b`
   conjunct with a language-neutral export/visibility notion derived from the
   diff content itself (added lines introducing an exported/public symbol across
   the languages `CODE_EXTENSIONS` already covers). Do NOT leave `\bpub\b` in
   place behind any generalized path check — the signal would stay confidently
   false in every non-Rust repo (see Context). The same rule applies to
   `userFacing`: derive it from content, not from path spelling.
3. Apply the fail-open policy for what content cannot decide: a signal that
   cannot be computed must NOT resolve to a confident `false`. Make it
   **genuinely absent** so the `signals == null` fail-open path engages — the
   current silent-false is exactly the `publicApiChanged` bug. Symmetrically, a
   signal must not resolve to a confident **`true`** off an incidental path-name
   match: **drop the generic `mcp`/`config` patterns from
   `USER_FACING_PATH_PATTERNS`** so `changelog` stops firing on
   `webpack.config.js` or `vite.config.ts` in an unrelated repo.
   **Scope the policy: "undeterminable" applies only when the diff actually
   touches code files (`codeFiles.length > 0`, already computed just above the
   return).** A docs-only diff is a genuine negative, not an undeterminable
   signal — it must keep resolving to `false` so the three surviving docs-only
   assertions listed in Context §1 stay legitimately green and the fail-open rule
   cannot widen into "run every dimension on every diff".
4. **Rebuild `securitySurface` on content triggering — this is the phase-2 handoff,
   now decided (see the operator decision above).** Phase 2 leaves
   `securitySurface` triggering on `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` alone as an explicitly
   interim state; this phase replaces that with a language-neutral content trigger
   over the diff — sink-shaped and capability-shaped tokens (process/command
   execution, filesystem access, environment and secret reads, deserialization,
   raw memory access) across the languages `CODE_EXTENSIONS` covers — and
   **removes `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` as a trigger**, for the same reason the
   `mcp`/`config` patterns go in step 3: a path-name convention fires on spelling
   coincidence in an unrelated repo and stays silent in a repo that spells things
   differently. Note this supersedes the interim path-based trigger assertions
   phase 2 adds; re-fixture them here per step 5, and correct phase 3's Context
   line that expected `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` to "survive largely intact" — under
   this decision it does not survive. The undeterminable/fail-open rule from step 3
   applies to `securitySurface` too.
5. Re-fixture the rdm-crate-path assertions in all three harnesses
   (`scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh`, `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh`,
   `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh`) onto the synthetic non-rdm
   project used by the acceptance criteria below. Rewrite
   `verify-workflow-review.sh:866-874`'s no-input `deepEqual` to encode the new
   no-configuration-present behavior rather than the old confident-false.
   **Leave the three docs-only non-triggering assertions UNCHANGED**
   (`verify-workflow-review.sh:797-801`,
   `verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh:340-344`,
   `verify-workflow-dispatch.sh:812-814`): they declare no paths at all, so
   re-fixturing them onto a synthetic project does not apply, and under step 3's
   code-files scoping they remain correct as written. If any of them goes red, the
   bug is in step 3's scoping, not in the assertion — fix the policy, do not
   delete the negative-path coverage.
6. Re-run `scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh`, then **copy the regenerated
   `.claude/workflows/{review-refute-fix,dispatch-phase}.js` over
   `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/`**. Do NOT change the propagation
   mechanism here: phase 2 of this roadmap commits to the same hand copy, and
   `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` is hand-maintained by design (the
   generator's consumer list and the shipped-template set are not the same three
   files — `plan-review.js` has no template and `autopilot.js` is stamped by a
   different generator). Unifying the generator over the shipped templates is a
   separate build-architecture item, not part of this phase.
7. **Verify the driver call sites need NO change, and assert it.** Under the
   content-derivation decision this phase adds no `deriveSignals` input, so the
   arg-threading sweep an earlier draft required is out of scope. Confirm rather
   than assume: `deriveSignals`' two callers sit BELOW the stamped markers and pass

8. **Update `docs/workflow-schemas.md`** — CLAUDE.md names it the canonical home

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No `rdm-cli`, `rdm-server`, or `rdm-core/src/` literal remains in
      `deriveSignals` or any stamped consumer — and no `\bpub\b` (or other
      Rust-only keyword) content clause remains in `publicApiChanged`
- [ ] **No declared-path or project-config channel is introduced.** `deriveSignals`'
      input shape is still exactly `{ targetType, changedFiles, diffText }`, and
      `grep -n 'deriveSignals(' .claude/workflows/*.js` shows both call sites
      unchanged. Every signal is computed from `diffText`/`changedFiles` content
- [ ] Given a synthetic non-rdm diff whose CONTENT introduces an exported symbol —
      `deriveSignals({ changedFiles: ['src/api/index.ts'], diffText: '+export function foo() {}\n' })`
      with NO project declaration of any kind — `publicApiChanged` is true and the
      `api-docs` dimension is selected. The test MUST supply a non-null `diffText`,
      because a `diffText`-omitting fixture takes the `diffText === null`
      short-circuit and reads true even when a Rust-only content clause survives
- [ ] Given a synthetic non-rdm diff whose content is user-facing, `userFacing` is
      true and the `changelog` dimension is selected — again with no declaration
- [ ] **Security triggers on content, not paths (closes phase 2's handoff):** a
      seeded non-Rust diff introducing a process-execution sink (e.g.
      `+const { exec } = require('child_process')` / `+exec(userInput)`) in a path
      matching NO security-sounding convention — `src/lib/runner.js` — yields
      `securitySurface: true` and `selectDimensions('code', …)` includes `security`.
      Conversely `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS` no longer exists: a repo-wide grep for it
      returns no hits, and a diff touching `src/auth/session.js` with no sink-shaped
      content does NOT trigger on the path name alone. The interim path-based
      trigger assertions phase 2 adds are re-fixtured onto these
- [ ] With content that decides nothing, an undeterminable signal does not resolve
      to a confident false — proven by a test asserting the dimension is still
      selected. `verify-workflow-review.sh:866-874`'s no-input `deepEqual` is
      rewritten to assert this, not the old `false`/`false`
- [ ] A **docs-only** diff (no code files) still selects ONLY the always-on set:
      `deriveSignals({ changedFiles: ['docs/foo.md'] })` leaves the conditional
      signals `false`, and the three existing docs-only assertions
      (`verify-workflow-review.sh:797-801`,
      `verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh:340-344`,
      `verify-workflow-dispatch.sh:812-814`) pass unmodified. This pins step 3's
      scoping so the fail-open policy cannot widen into always running every
      dimension
- [ ] No confident-TRUE off an incidental path-name match either: for a synthetic
      non-rdm diff touching ONLY `webpack.config.js` (a path matching the old
      generic `config` pattern) whose content is not user-facing, `userFacing` is
      NOT confidently `true` by virtue of that match — it takes whatever value
      step 3's undeterminable-signal policy dictates, identically to a diff
      touching only `src/util/helper.js`. A test pins the two cases to the same
      `userFacing` value, so the retired `config`/`mcp` patterns cannot be
      reintroduced
- [ ] `docs/workflow-schemas.md`'s `deriveSignals(input)` /
      `selectDimensions(mode, signals)` sections match the post-change code:
      content-derived signals, no `SECURITY_PATH_PATTERNS`, and the
      fully-populated-vs-absent signal invariant
- [ ] `selectDimensions`' three-way fail-open contract is unchanged, with its
      existing tests still passing
- [ ] `CODE_EXTENSIONS` is untouched
- [ ] `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{review-refute-fix,dispatch-phase}.js`
      are byte-identical to the regenerated `.claude/workflows/` copies
- [ ] All four gates pass, including the planted-mutation self-tests on the signal

Two structural concerns from plan review are NOT settled by this document and are

- `task/resolve-security-surface-trigger-scope` — phase 2 assigns

- `task/decide-derive-signals-config-delivery` — step 2's "phase 1 config

  fetch changes this phase's file set, its Rust test surface, and its size.

coherence.concern: Step 3's core mechanism — make an undeterminable signal "genuinely ABSENT" so "selectDimensions' existing `signals == null` fail-open path engages" — is mechanically impossible against the code it names, and produces the exact silent-drop bug the phase exists to remove.
coherence.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals — "Operator decision" bullet 2 and Step 3; vs .claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs:595-603 (selectDimensions) and :165/:178/:192 (the `when` predicates)
coherence.what_fails: `selectDimensions(mode, signals)` tests `if (signals == null) return dims.slice()` on the WHOLE signals object. `deriveSignals` always returns an object, so omitting one key never reaches that branch. Control then falls to `dims.filter((d) => !d.when || d.when(signals))` with predicates `(s) => !!s.publicApiChanged`, `(s) => !!s.userFacing`, `(s) => !!(s.securitySurface || s.hasUnsafe)` — an absent key is `undefined`, `!!undefined` is false, and the dimension is DROPPED. An implementer following step 3 literally (delete the key when content cannot decide) ships a review that silently skips api-docs/changelog/security — the identical failure mode the Context calls "the most dangerous category in the roadmap". review.mjs:646-650 and docs/workflow-schemas.md:297-309 already state this outcome verbatim ("A partially-populated object would make a conditional dimension drop out on a MISSING key rather than a real negative"), and verify-workflow-review.sh:930-932 pins it with `assert.equal(typeof d1[key], 'boolean')` for every SIGNAL_KEY — an assertion step 5 does not list for re-fixturing.
coherence.why: The three reconciliations available lead to materially different shipped behavior, and the plan's own ACs rule out two of them: (a) set the undeterminable signal to `true` (keeps booleans, keeps selectDimensions untouched — but is not "absent" and is not the `signals == null` path the plan names); (b) make `when` read tri-state (`s.x !== false`) — which breaks AC "selectDimensions' three-way fail-open contract is unchanged, with its existing tests still passing", since verify-workflow-review.sh:872-877 asserts an explicit `{}` selects only `['ac','correctness']`; (c) change selectDimensions/SIGNAL_KEYS — likewise barred by that AC. The plan therefore simultaneously prescribes a mechanism, forbids every way of implementing it, and asserts an outcome ("a test asserting the dimension is still selected") that only mechanism (a) can satisfy.
coherence.recommendation: Decide the mechanism in the document before implementation. The only option consistent with the rest of the ACs is per-signal fail-open: keep `deriveSignals` returning a fully-populated boolean object and set an undeterminable conditional signal to `true` (so the dimension is selected), rather than deleting the key. Rewrite the "genuinely ABSENT / engages the `signals == null` path" wording in the Operator decision and step 3 to say that, keep `selectDimensions` and SIGNAL_KEYS untouched, and note that verify-workflow-review.sh:930-932's `typeof === 'boolean'` loop survives unchanged. If genuine absence really is wanted, the phase must also own the `when`-predicate/selectDimensions change and the AC forbidding it must be dropped — that is a larger phase.

coherence.concern: For a code-touching diff, the plan never says when a content-derived signal is a legitimate `false` versus "undeterminable". Read as written, step 3 makes every conditional dimension fire on every code diff, which nullifies the point of `deriveSignals` and contradicts step 3's own guard.
coherence.location: phase-3-generic-diff-signals — Step 3 ("'undeterminable' applies only when the diff actually touches code files (`codeFiles.length > 0`)") and ACs 6 and 7
coherence.what_fails: Step 3 scopes undeterminable to `codeFiles.length > 0` and carves out only docs-only diffs. So for a diff touching `src/util/helper.js` whose added lines contain no export, no user-facing token, and no sink: is `publicApiChanged` a confident `false` (content was read and found no added export) or undeterminable (the heuristic cannot prove the negative)? The plan does not say, and AC 7 explicitly refuses to pin it ("it takes whatever value step 3's undeterminable-signal policy dictates"). Under the undeterminable reading, api-docs + changelog + security are selected for essentially every code diff — precisely the "run every dimension on every diff" widening step 3 says must not happen, with only docs-only diffs excluded. Under the confident-false reading, the signals stay selective but AC 6's "undeterminable signal … dimension is still selected" has no non-docs case left to exercise.
coherence.why: The two branches produce opposite products from the same document: a selective content-derived gate, or a de facto always-run review whose per-dimension `when` predicates are dead code for any code diff. That is an outcome difference, not an implementation detail, and the harness re-fixturing in step 5 hardcodes whichever branch is chosen.
coherence.recommendation: State the rule explicitly, per signal. A workable form: a positive content match sets the signal `true`; the absence of a match over a diff that was actually READ (non-null `diffText`, code files present) is a legitimate `false`; only a diff whose content could not be read at all (`diffText === null` while `codeFiles.length > 0`, e.g. a truncated or unavailable diff) is undeterminable and fails open.
