# Phase 4: Parameterize the rdm binary and project as runtime arguments (monorepo-safe)

## Context

Absorbs `workflow-lane-hardening/phase-5-parameterize-workflow-scripts-rdm-binary`,
which covers only the mechanical half of this.

Every rdm invocation in the three shipped scripts hardcodes `./target/debug/rdm`,
and every *project-scoped* one hardcodes `--project rdm`. The raw counts differ
per file (dispatch-phase.js: 17 binary sites vs 7 `--project rdm` sites;
autopilot.js: 13 vs 12), but that delta is NOT a defect — it is exactly the
`rdm model resolve` calls, which is a project-agnostic subcommand that does not
accept `--project` at all (`./target/debug/rdm model resolve plan --project rdm`
errors with `unexpected argument '--project' found`). `rdm commit`/`status`/
`discard` are in the same class — CLAUDE.md already documents them as operating
on the whole plan repo's git state and taking no `--project`. So the current
state IS internally consistent, and this phase is purely a parameterization, not
a bug fix.

**Design revised after plan review.** The original emit-time `{rdm_bin}`
placeholder was unworkable: `.claude/workflows/*.js` is simultaneously the
template `generate_workflows()` `include_str!`s and the file the Workflow tool
executes, with no emit step in rdm's own loop — a placeholder would sit literally
unsubstituted in the file rdm itself runs. Both axes are therefore RUNTIME
arguments. See the roadmap body's Approach section.

Runtime args change no bytes, so the byte-identity gates
(`generate_workflows_are_byte_identical_to_source`, agent_config.rs:1249; section
3 of verify-agent-config-distribution.sh) stay valid and green. This phase does
NOT touch them.

**Read the roadmap's Scope section before editing anything** — the sites in this
phase span three different propagation mechanisms, and most live in hand-written
driver regions with no lib and no generator.

**Step 8 added (engine-name single-sourcing).** This phase now also collapses the
hardcoded workflow-engine *name* literals to one canonical list per lane. It is
placed here, and not in its own phase, because this phase already edits every
site that carries those literals — `agent_config.rs`'s `relative_path` values and
`include_str!` paths, `verify-agent-config-distribution.sh`'s pinned `WORKFLOWS`
list, and the generator consumer lists. Phase 7 renames all seven engines to
`rdm-wf-*`; without step 8 that rename must correctly edit ~30 scattered literal
sites in lockstep, which is what made the superseded
`workflow-lane-hardening/phase-1-prefix-workflow-engines-to-distinguish-from-skills`
unplannable (three failed dispatches; the plan author died twice at 83 events
mid-sweep). With step 8, phase 7 edits one list plus the file moves.

## Steps

1. Add a `projectFlag(cfg)` helper (shape per `.claude/workflows/backlog.js:115`)
   and an `rdmBin` resolver defaulting to `rdm`. Place them per the mechanism that
   owns each region — respecting the no-import constraint, which means the helper
   may need to exist in more than one region rather than being shared.
   `projectFlag(cfg)` is applied ONLY at the call sites that build
   project-scoped commands. The project-agnostic allow-list — sites that must
   carry NO project flag — is `rdm model resolve` and `rdm commit` (plus
   `status`/`discard` if ever added). Every other subcommand used in these
   scripts (`phase list/show/update`, `task list/show/create/update`,
   `worktree add`, `next`, `search`) is project-scoped and takes the flag.
2. Replace every `./target/debug/rdm` and `--project rdm` literal, working region
   by region per the roadmap's Scope section: generator-stamped libs first, then
   byte-identical copies in lockstep, then the driver regions directly.
3. Parse `project` and `rdmBin` in `parseAutopilotArgs` and dispatch-phase's arg
   parsing, and thread both through `workflow('dispatch-phase', payload)` in
   autopilot.js — the ONLY `workflow(...)` call in the tree (autopilot.js:1008).
   Without this the nested run silently drops to the ambient default and can drive
   a same-named roadmap in the WRONG project. Note that dispatch-phase does NOT
   invoke review-refute-fix via `workflow()`: it consumes `lib/review.mjs` as a
   compile-time stamped block. review-refute-fix.js is a sibling top-level
   workflow reached only from the `rdm-review` skill, so its parameters are wired
   by step 4, not by nesting. Do not add a `workflow()` call inside dispatch-phase
   — that would exceed the documented one-level nesting budget.
4. Add `--project <name>` / `rdmBin` passing to EVERY skill shim that invokes any
   workflow this phase parameterizes — the three shipped scripts AND `estimate.js`
   (in scope per step 6) — in both the shipped templates and the local dogfood
   copies, and have rdm's own shims pass `./target/debug/rdm` as `rdmBin`:
   - `rdm-autopilot` and `rdm-dispatch-phase` (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` +
     `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-{autopilot,dispatch-phase}-{cli,mcp}.md`)
   - `rdm-do` — its `--auto` phase and task flows both invoke `dispatch-phase`
     (`.claude/skills/rdm-do/SKILL.md:87,101` +
     `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-do-{cli,mcp}.md`)
   - `rdm-review` — the only caller of `review-refute-fix`
     (`.claude/skills/rdm-review/SKILL.md:40-43` +
     `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-review-{cli,mcp}.md`)
   - `rdm-estimate` — the only caller of `estimate.js`, which today invokes it
     with `{ roadmap, phase }` and nothing else
     (`.claude/skills/rdm-estimate/SKILL.md:26`). **Local dogfood copy only**:
     `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-estimate-{cli,mcp}.md` is still the
     prose rating loop with `{proj_flag}` emit-time substitution, NOT a workflow
     shim, so it needs no change here. Without this bullet, zeroing the literals

accept `--project` at all (`./target/debug/rdm model resolve plan --project rdm`
errors with `unexpected argument '--project' found`). `rdm commit`/`status`/
`discard` are in the same class — CLAUDE.md already documents them as operating
on the whole plan repo's git state and taking no `--project`. So the current
state IS internally consistent, and this phase is purely a parameterization, not
a bug fix.

**Design revised after plan review.** The original emit-time `{rdm_bin}`
placeholder was unworkable: `.claude/workflows/*.js` is simultaneously the
template `generate_workflows()` `include_str!`s and the file the Workflow tool
executes, with no emit step in rdm's own loop — a placeholder would sit literally
unsubstituted in the file rdm itself runs. Both axes are therefore RUNTIME
arguments. See the roadmap body's Approach section.

Runtime args change no bytes, so the byte-identity gates
(`generate_workflows_are_byte_identical_to_source`, agent_config.rs:1249; section
3 of verify-agent-config-distribution.sh) stay valid and green. This phase does
NOT touch them.

**Read the roadmap's Scope section before editing anything** — the sites in this
phase span three different propagation mechanisms, and most live in hand-written
driver regions with no lib and no generator.

hardcoded workflow-engine *name* literals to one canonical list per lane. It is
placed here, and not in its own phase, because this phase already edits every
site that carries those literals — `agent_config.rs`'s `relative_path` values and

target:
phase project-agnostic-lane/phase-6-cleanup-superseded-emitted-workflows

## Context

**This phase is a prerequisite for phase 7's rename.** It must land first.

`rdm-cli`'s workflow write path writes each file by its `relative_path` and never removes files it did not emit (`write_workflows` in `rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs`, plus `rdm-cli`'s `--out` wiring). Today that is harmless: the emitted set never shrinks and no file is ever superseded.

Phase 7 breaks that assumption. After the engines are renamed to `rdm-wf-*`, a downstream repo that already ran `rdm agent-config claude --skills --out <dir>` and re-runs it gets the three new files written alongside the three old ones:

    .claude/workflows/autopilot.js            <- stale, still present
    .claude/workflows/rdm-wf-autopilot.js     <- newly emitted

Both parse, both register, and both surface in the skill/slash-command listing with identical descriptions. The rename's entire purpose is to remove ambiguity from that listing, so shipping it without cleanup leaves downstream users strictly worse off than before — two indistinguishable entries per engine instead of one confusing one. This is the hazard the superseded `workflow-lane-hardening/phase-1-...` body flagged as "pick one and state it"; this phase is where it gets picked.

## Decision

**Implement cleanup in the write path (option (a)).** The alternative — a CHANGELOG migration note telling users to `rm` the old files by hand — was rejected: it is silently skippable, it leaves the broken state as the default for anyone who does not read the changelog, and `agent-config` is exactly the command a user runs expecting the emitted lane to be correct afterwards.

## Safety constraints — read before implementing

Deleting files inside a user's repository is destructive and irreversible from rdm's side. The implementation must be conservative:

- **Remove only from an explicit, hardcoded superseded-name set.** Never "remove anything in the output directory that rdm did not just emit" — a user may keep their own scripts alongside the emitted ones, and a blanket sweep would destroy them.
- **Scope the removal to the workflows output directory** that this invocation writes to. Do not walk parents or siblings.
- **Only remove a file rdm plausibly wrote.** Before unlinking, confirm the file's content matches a known previously-emitted version of that engine. A file at `autopilot.js` that the user has since edited must NOT be silently deleted — leave it and report it.
- **Report every removal and every skip on stdout**, so the user sees what `agent-config` did to their tree.
- **Never fail the emit because a removal failed.** A permission error on cleanup reports and continues; the newly emitted files are the primary contract.

## Steps

1. Add a superseded-name table to `agent_config.rs`, paired with the canonical engine-name table introduced by phase 4 step 8: for each engine, its current emitted `relative_path` and the list of names it has previously been emitted under. At this phase's start that list is empty for every engine — phase 7 populates it with the pre-rename bare names. Land the mechanism here with the table empty, and a test proving an empty table removes nothing.
2. Extend the write path to consult that table after writing: for each superseded name that exists in the output directory, apply the safety constraints above, then remove or skip-and-report.
3. Surface the outcome in `rdm-cli`'s `agent-config` output: a line per removed file and a distinct line per skipped-because-modified file.
4. Extend `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` with a section that emits into a temp dir, plants a superseded-named file, re-emits, and asserts the stale file is gone; plants a *modified* superseded-named file and asserts it survives with a report; and plants an unrelated user file and asserts it is untouched.
5. Add a planted-corruption self-test proving the new gate is not vacuous: disabling the cleanup call turns the harness red.
6. CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] describing the new cleanup behavior of `rdm agent-config` — user-facing, so it ships in this commit per the project's changelog rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A superseded-name table exists, paired with phase 4's canonical engine-name table, and is EMPTY at this phase's completion (phase 7 populates it)
- [ ] With an empty table, `agent-config` removes nothing — asserted by a test
- [ ] Given a superseded-named file whose content matches a known emitted version, re-emitting removes it and reports the removal
- [ ] Given a superseded-named file the user has MODIFIED, re-emitting leaves it in place and reports it as skipped — asserted explicitly, since silent deletion of user edits is the primary risk this phase carries
- [ ] An unrelated user-authored file in the same output directory is never touched
- [ ] A failed removal (e.g. permissions) reports and does not fail the emit; the newly emitted files still land
- [ ] Removal is scoped to the workflows output directory of the current invocation — no parent or sibling traversal
- [ ] `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` covers all of the above, and a planted-corruption self-test proves the new section is not vacuous
- [ ] The byte-identity gates remain GREEN and untouched
- [ ] `cargo nextest run`, `cargo test -p rdm-core --doc`, and every `scripts/verify-*.sh` pass
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased]

phase project-agnostic-lane/phase-7-prefix-workflow-engines

## Context

Absorbs `workflow-lane-hardening/phase-1-prefix-workflow-engines-to-distinguish-from-skills`, which is `wont-fix` with a pointer here. It moved because the rename touches the same files phases 4 and 6 already rewrite — doing it there would rewrite that surface twice.

**Depends on phase 4 step 8 and phase 6. Do not start before both have landed.** Phase 4 step 8 collapses the scattered engine-name literals to one canonical list per lane, which is what makes this phase a small diff. Phase 6 lands the superseded-name cleanup mechanism with an empty table; this phase populates it.

## Problem

The workflow-lane engines under `.claude/workflows/` surface with **bare names** in the skill / slash-command listing, colliding conceptually with their `rdm-*` skill front doors. A user asked "to run autopilot do I use `/autopilot` or `/rdm-autopilot`?" — the answer (`rdm-autopilot` is the front door; `autopilot` is the engine it drives via the Workflow tool) is not inferable from the names. Five of the seven engines have an identically-worded `rdm-*` front door.

## Decisions — settled, do not relitigate

- **The prefix is `rdm-wf-`.** Chosen over a bare `wf-` so every rdm-provided listing entry shares the one `rdm-` namespace and sorts together, and so the prefix stays unambiguous in a repo with its own unrelated `wf-*` tooling.
- **The seven new engine names are exactly:** `rdm-wf-autopilot`, `rdm-wf-dispatch-phase`, `rdm-wf-review-refute-fix`, `rdm-wf-backlog`, `rdm-wf-document`, `rdm-wf-estimate`, `rdm-wf-plan-review`.
- **All seven move in one commit.** A prefix scheme applied to a subset is worse than none, because a reader can no longer infer from the *absence* of a prefix whether a listing entry is a skill or an engine. This forecloses splitting by engine subset.
- **`.claude/workflows/lib/*.mjs` filenames do NOT change.** They are shared source libraries, not engines, and never surface in the listing. Their `//!`/header path comments naming their `.js` consumers DO change, and the byte-identity drift gates pair lib to consumer by path, so those gate paths change even though the lib filenames do not.
- **The `rdm-*` skill front-door names do NOT change.** `rdm-autopilot`, `rdm-dispatch-phase`, `rdm-review`, `rdm-land`, `rdm-do`, `rdm-estimate`, `rdm-backlog`, `rdm-document`, `rdm-plan-review` all keep their names. This is the single most dangerous confusion in the sweep — see the warning below.

## The reference surface — precomputed, do not re-derive

The superseded phase asked its planner to re-derive this with a broad `grep -rln`. That sweep matched 124 files / 2,710 lines because `document`, `estimate`, `backlog`, and `plan-review` are ordinary English words that appear throughout the prose. Three dispatch attempts failed, the plan author dying twice at exactly 83 events mid-sweep. **The actual rename surface is 46 files.** It is enumerated below. Verify it is still current with the targeted greps in "Reference forms", but do not start from a bare word grep.

### WARNING — the front-door/engine name collision

`rdm-autopilot` (skill, unchanged) contains `autopilot` (engine, renamed) as a substring. A naive `s/autopilot/rdm-wf-autopilot/` corrupts every skill name into `rdm-rdm-wf-autopilot`, in ~40 files. The same trap applies to all five engines with a same-named front door. Every substitution must be anchored to a reference *form* below, never to the bare word.

### Reference forms — the six ways an engine is named

1. **Path references** `.claude/workflows/<name>.js` — the bulk of the surface.
2. **`meta.name` declarations** in each engine: `name: '<name>',` — a co-equal source of the listing entry alongside the filename, and the reference most likely to be missed, leaving the listing showing the old bare name.
3. **Nested `workflow('<name>', …)` calls** — `autopilot.js` invokes `workflow('dispatch-phase', …)` and the estimate pre-pass. This is the only `workflow()` call in the tree.

## Context

Absorbs `workflow-lane-hardening/phase-1-prefix-workflow-engines-to-distinguish-from-skills`, which is `wont-fix` with a pointer here. It moved because the rename touches the same files phases 4 and 6 already rewrite — doing it there would rewrite that surface twice.

**Depends on phase 4 step 8 and phase 6. Do not start before both have landed.** Phase 4 step 8 collapses the scattered engine-name literals to one canonical list per lane, which is what makes this phase a small diff. Phase 6 lands the superseded-name cleanup mechanism with an empty table; this phase populates it.

## Problem

The workflow-lane engines under `.claude/workflows/` surface with **bare names** in the skill / slash-command listing, colliding conceptually with their `rdm-*` skill front doors. A user asked "to run autopilot do I use `/autopilot` or `/rdm-autopilot`?" — the answer (`rdm-autopilot` is the front door; `autopilot` is the engine it drives via the Workflow tool) is not inferable from the names. Five of the seven engines have an identically-worded `rdm-*` front door.

## Decisions — settled, do not relitigate

- **The prefix is `rdm-wf-`.** Chosen over a bare `wf-` so every rdm-provided listing entry shares the one `rdm-` namespace and sorts together, and so the prefix stays unambiguous in a repo with its own unrelated `wf-*` tooling.
- **The seven new engine names are exactly:** `rdm-wf-autopilot`, `rdm-wf-dispatch-phase`, `rdm-wf-review-refute-fix`, `rdm-wf-backlog`, `rdm-wf-document`, `rdm-wf-estimate`, `rdm-wf-plan-review`.
- **All seven move in one commit.** A prefix scheme applied to a subset is worse than none, because a reader can no longer infer from the *absence* of a prefix whether a listing entry is a skill or an engine. This forecloses splitting by engine subset.
- **`.claude/workflows/lib/*.mjs` filenames do NOT change.** They are shared source libraries, not engines, and never surface in the listing. Their `//!`/header path comments naming their `.js` consumers DO change, and the byte-identity drift gates pair lib to consumer by path, so those gate paths change even though the lib filenames do not.
- **The `rdm-*` skill front-door names do NOT change.** `rdm-autopilot`, `rdm-dispatch-phase`, `rdm-review`, `rdm-land`, `rdm-do`, `rdm-estimate`, `rdm-backlog`, `rdm-document`, `rdm-plan-review` all keep their names. This is the single most dangerous confusion in the sweep — see the warning below.

## The reference surface — precomputed, do not re-derive

The superseded phase asked its planner to re-derive this with a broad `grep -rln`. That sweep matched 124 files / 2,710 lines because `document`, `estimate`, `backlog`, and `plan-review` are ordinary English words that appear throughout the prose. Three dispatch attempts failed, the plan author dying twice at exactly 83 events mid-sweep. **The actual rename surface is 46 files.** It is enumerated below. Verify it is still current with the targeted greps in "Reference forms", but do not start from a bare word grep.

### WARNING — the front-door/engine name collision

`rdm-autopilot` (skill, unchanged) contains `autopilot` (engine, renamed) as a substring. A naive `s/autopilot/rdm-wf-autopilot/` corrupts every skill name into `rdm-rdm-wf-autopilot`, in ~40 files. The same trap applies to all five engines with a same-named front door. Every substitution must be anchored to a reference *form* below, never to the bare word.

### Reference forms — the six ways an engine is named

1. **Path references** `.claude/workflows/<name>.js` — the bulk of the surface.
2. **`meta.name` declarations** in each engine: `name: '<name>',` — a co-equal source of the listing entry alongside the filename, and the reference most likely to be missed, leaving the listing showing the old bare name.
3. **Nested `workflow('<name>', …)` calls** — `autopilot.js` invokes `workflow('dispatch-phase', …)` and the estimate pre-pass. This is the only `workflow()` call in the tree.
4. **`Workflow({ name: '<name>' })` object invocations.**
5. **Bare prose-form invocation** — `.claude/skills/rdm-review/SKILL.md:43` is a standalone line reading `Workflow: review-refute-fix`. This form matches none of the above greps; it was missed by the first two sweeps and must be handled explicitly.
6. **Shipped template copies** `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/<name>.js` — only three engines are shipped: `autopilot.js`, `dispatch-phase.js`, `review-refute-fix.js`.

    grep -rnE "^Workflow:\s*($N)\s*$" .claude rdm-core/src/templates

### Files to change (46)

The way a shim actually names the engine it invokes is backticked prose without the path or extension: `.claude/skills/rdm-autopilot/SKILL.md:9` ("by invoking the **`autopilot` Workflow**"), `:29` ("**Invoke the `autopilot` workflow** via the Workflow tool"), `:31` ("the `dispatch-phase` workflow"). coherence.concern: Step 3 / AC 2 require EXECUTING the emitted pipeline's pure logic (`deriveSignals`, `selectDimensions`, the command builders), but the emitted workflow scripts are not loadable by Node and expose none of those functions — and the plan names no extraction mechanism.
coherence.location: project-agnostic-lane/phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Steps 3 and 3a; AC 2 and AC 4 ("EXECUTES the emitted pipeline's pure logic", "command built by the emitted scripts")
coherence.what_fails: The emitted artifacts are `.claude/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` (only these three are in `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/`; `lib/*.mjs` is explicitly unshipped). Each file's only export is `export const meta` (dispatch-phase.js:25) and each ends in a top-level `return` (dispatch-phase.js:1769 `return outcome`) because the Workflow runtime wraps the file body in a function. Dynamically importing an emitted copy fails outright: `node -e "import('/tmp/dp-test.js')"` → `SyntaxError: Illegal return statement`. `deriveSignals` (dispatch-phase.js:631), `selectDimensions` (:573), and the prompt/command builders (`buildFetchPrompt` :1348, `buildStampInProgressPrompt` :1393) are module-private. So an implementer following step 3 as written cannot drive them from the emitted tree; the path of least resistance is to import this repo's `lib/review.mjs` / `lib/dispatch-phase.mjs` instead — which are NOT emitted, so the harness would once again certify a local artifact rather than the downstream one, the exact 'held the disproof in its hands' failure this phase exists to close.
coherence.why: The phase's entire value is proving the EMITTED lane works downstream. If the executed code is not the emitted bytes, AC 2/AC 4 pass while the stated gap remains open, and the planted-corruption self-test in step 4 would be planted into the wrong file too.
coherence.recommendation: Name the extraction mechanism in step 3: copy each emitted `.js` into the fixture scratch dir, strip/neutralize the trailing top-level `return`, append an explicit `export { deriveSignals, selectDimensions, buildFetchPrompt, ... }` block, write it as `.mjs`, and dynamic-import THAT — asserting the source of the copy is the emitted file, never `.claude/workflows/lib/*.mjs`. Add an AC clause forbidding the harness from importing anything under `.claude/workflows/lib/`, so the fallback cannot silently satisfy the gate.

coherence.concern: AC 3 ("Every rdm command built during that run names the fixture's binary and project") contradicts the roadmap's own project-agnostic allow-list, under which some built commands must carry NO project flag.
coherence.location: project-agnostic-lane/phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Acceptance Criteria, bullet 3
coherence.what_fails: The roadmap's Problem §2 states "a script's binary-call count legitimately EXCEEDS its project-flag count: `rdm model resolve` (like `rdm commit`/`status`/`discard`) is project-agnostic and rejects `--project` outright... the parameterization must preserve it", and phase 4 step 1 pins the allow-list explicitly. Verified against the real binary: `./target/debug/rdm model resolve plan --project rdm` → `error: unexpected argument '--project' found`. dispatch-phase.js builds five such commands (:1358-1364, :1379-1383). An implementer encoding AC 3 literally as "every built command contains ` --project <fixture>`" gets a harness that goes red on well-formed `model resolve`/`commit` lines, and the obvious 'fix' is to add the flag in the workflow scripts — breaking the lane the harness is supposed to validate.
coherence.why: The AC states a universal that the roadmap elsewhere states is false; only one of the two can be implemented, and the wrong choice produces commands the CLI rejects.
coherence.recommendation: Reword AC 3 to: every built command names the fixture's binary, and every PROJECT-SCOPED command names the fixture's project, with `rdm model resolve` / `rdm commit` / `status` / `discard` asserted to carry no `--project` at all; keep the `zero ./target/debug/rdm or --project rdm occurrences` clause as-is.

coherence.concern: Step 1 does not require the fixture plan repo to be seeded with a roadmap/phase, yet AC 4 requires a built command executed against it to exit 0 with the expected output shape.
coherence.location: project-agnostic-lane/phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Step 1 vs Step 3a / AC 4
coherence.what_fails:
Step 1 asks only for "its own plan repo, project name, and a small source tree". The commands these scripts build are item-scoped (`rdm phase show --roadmap --project

--format json`, `rdm task show ...`, `rdm phase update ... --status in-progress`). Run against an empty plan repo they exit non-zero, so AC 4 is unsatisfiable without a seeding step. Step 3a's own model, `scripts/verify-workflow-estimate.sh`, does seed (its hermetic-seed section creates a roadmap plus phases with the real binary before feeding output back through the pure functions), so the omission is in step 1's wording rather than in the intent. Step 1 likewise never says the fixture gets its own rdm binary at a non-`target/debug` path, which step 3a's "the fixture's own binary path" presumes.
coherence.why: Leaving both prerequisites implicit invites an under-built fixture that forces the implementer to weaken AC 4 to a command that needs no plan data.
coherence.recommendation: Extend step 1: initialize the fixture plan repo as a git repo, create at least one roadmap with one phase (and one task) under the fixture project name using the real binary, and place the binary at a fixture-owned path (copy or symlink into the temp tree) so `rdmBin` is demonstrably not `./target/debug/rdm`.

architectural-fit.concern: Step 3 / AC-2 require the harness to EXECUTE the emitted pipeline's pure logic (`deriveSignals`, `selectDimensions`, the command builders) out of the emitted tree, but the emitted artifacts are Workflow scripts that Node cannot load, and the only Node-loadable form (`lib/*.mjs`) is deliberately not emitted. The plan names no extraction mechanism, so the AC is either unimplementable or will be silently satisfied by driving this repo's `lib/*.mjs` — which reintroduces exactly the necessary-but-not-sufficient gap the phase exists to close.
architectural-fit.location: phase project-agnostic-lane/phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Steps 3 and 3a; AC "The harness EXECUTES the emitted pipeline's pure logic"
architectural-fit.what_fails: `rdm agent-config claude --skills --out <dir>` emits only `.js` workflow scripts (rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs:353-363 lists exactly three `WorkflowFile`s: autopilot.js, dispatch-phase.js, review-refute-fix.js — no `lib/`). Those files end in a top-level `return` (`.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:1769`, `autopilot.js:1032`, `review-refute-fix.js:1080`) and reference ambient globals (`args`, `agent`, `pipeline`, `log`). Importing one in Node fails outright: `import('.../.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js')` -> `SyntaxError: Illegal return statement` (verified, node v24.18.0). Every existing harness sidesteps this by importing the un-emitted lib module instead — `verify-workflow-estimate.sh`'s hermetic-seed section, which step 3a says to model on, runs `run_node "$TMP/real.mjs" "$LIB"` where `$LIB` is `.claude/workflows/lib/estimate.mjs`, not the emitted `estimate.js`. So an implementer following step 3 literally hits a SyntaxError on the fixture's emitted files, and the path of least resistance is to import `<repo>/.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` and declare the emitted lane exercised — proving something about a file the downstream repo never receives, bridged only by the byte-identity chain this phase's own Context calls insufficient.
architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md's Workflow-tool section states as a proven constraint that "The Workflow runtime cannot `import`/`require`", and the corollary file shape (top-level driver code, ambient globals, top-level `return`) is what makes the emitted scripts non-importable. The plan step assumes the emitted artifacts behave like the lib modules, which the architecture forbids. Because the phase's entire thesis is that byte-identity is necessary-but-not-sufficient, quietly substituting the lib module for the emitted script makes the new gate circular and the AC vacuous — the same failure mode the phase was written to fix.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Name the mechanism in the plan. Either (a) extract from the FIXTURE's emitted `.js` — slice the `>>> review-refute-fix:begin/end <<<` and `>>> dispatch-outcome:begin/end <<<` marker blocks out of the emitted file, append an `export { deriveSignals, selectDimensions, ... }` shim, write it to the fixture temp dir, and `import()` that, so the bytes under test provably came from the emission; or (b) state explicitly that the harness drives `lib/*.mjs` and add a gate proving the emitted `.js` still contains those exact marker blocks byte-for-byte, so the substitution is a stated, checked bridge rather than an unstated assumption. architectural-fit.concern: Step 3a requires running a built command "using the fixture's own binary path" and AC-3 forbids any `./target/debug/rdm` occurrence, but the plan never says what the fixture binary actually is. The two obvious readings each break a stated rule: PATH-resolved bare `rdm` violates the dev-build requirement and breaks hermeticity, while a stub script makes the exit-0 assertion vacuous.
architectural-fit.location: phase project-agnostic-lane/phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Step 3a; AC "Every rdm command built during that run names the fixture's binary and project; zero `./target/debug/rdm` or `--project rdm` occurrences" and AC "...exits 0 with the expected output shape"
architectural-fit.what_fails: Phase 4's design (roadmap Approach) makes `args.rdmBin` default to bare `rdm` on PATH. architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md's dev-build rule and the harnesses' hermeticity convention both constrain which binary a verify script may execute. architectural-fit.concern: Steps 5 and 6 require sweeping and editing plan-repo bodies (the `resolve-workflow-byte-identity-before-substitution` task, `workflow-lane-hardening` phases 1 and 5) but never name the access mechanism, and the repo has a hard rule that plan data may only be touched via the CLI.
architectural-fit.location: phase project-agnostic-lane/phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Step 5 ("The sweep covers PLAN-REPO BODIES as well as source and docs") and Step 6; AC "a repo-wide sweep — source, docs, AND plan-repo bodies"
architectural-fit.what_fails: "Repo-wide sweep" plus "plan-repo bodies" invites `grep -r "$RDM_ROOT"`, and "Update the note" / "rewrite that sentence" invites editing the markdown under `~/Projects/rdm-atlas-repo` directly. restraint.concern: The plan pins stale-doc targets to exact line numbers (`agent_config.rs:236-238`, `README.md:93`, `CLAUDE.md:176`) and hardens one of them into an acceptance criterion, in a phase that is explicitly ordered to run LAST — after phases 4, 6 and 7 have restructured those very files.
restraint.location: phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Steps 5, and AC bullet "`agent_config.rs:236-238` no longer gives the import limitation as the reason for absent substitution"
restraint.what_fails: I verified the citations are accurate against today's `main`: the `WorkflowFile` doc comment sits at rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs:234-239, the README paragraph at README.md:93, the CLAUDE.md paragraph at 176. restraint.location: phase-8-downstream-execution-harness — Steps 6, and the corresponding AC bullet on `workflow-lane-hardening` phase 5's wont-fix note
restraint.what_fails: Step 5 already says: "The sweep covers PLAN-REPO BODIES as well as source and docs, and covers both stale claims — the import-limitation non-sequitur AND the superseded emit-time `{rdm_bin}` placeholder design." Original scope items 1 and 2 are **done**; items 3, 4 and 6 are superseded by what the run found. What remains is below.

## What the run settled (do not redo)

- **`agentType` Workflow-path resolution is UNVERIFIED — the spike's `agentType` cases were INVALID and their apparent negative is RETRACTED.** Cases B and F raised `agent type 'rdm-mechanical' not found`, and this was first recorded as a measured negative. It is not one. The run was dispatched from a session rooted at the main checkout, whose project root had NO `.claude/agents/` directory at session start; the definition was copied in mid-session. Claude Code's subagent docs name this as a restart case: the watcher "covers only directories that existed when the session started, so after creating a scope's first agent file in a new `agents` directory, restart to load it." The definition was never loaded. The retry probe re-tested the same unwatched directory. Project subagents are also discovered by walking up from the CWD, so the worktree's own committed `.claude/agents/` was never in scope for a session rooted elsewhere. **Cases B/F say nothing about `agent({ agentType })`.**
- **An id absent from the registry RAISES** — this part stands, on case C alone (a deliberately unknown id, independent of our definition). Contrast an unknown `model` id, which resolves `agent()` to `null` silently.
- **`effort: 'low'` passed to `agent()` IS honored** — spike case E recorded `effort: "low"`, the first such record in a 156384-record corpus, while the four sibling cases in the same run recorded `"high"`. This REVERSES the earlier definition-side negative (declaring `effort:` in agent frontmatter is accepted and not honored). The two routes genuinely differ.
- **An invalid `effort` value is accepted and silently degrades to `high`** — it does not throw. Opposite failure mode to `agentType`.
- Scope item 3 could **not** be exercised (does `agent(prompt,{schema})` survive the restricted `tools:` list; is `agentType` honored through `parallel()`) — nothing ever resolved, so nothing ran under the definition.
- **The 15 local-only mechanical sites ARE now threaded** (commit 695b2ac), and the surface is enumerated in `docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md` § "The threadable surface, enumerated" — 15 sites across `document.js`, `backlog.js`, `estimate.js`, `plan-review.js`, with their three maintenance routes and the judgment-site exclusions. Reuse that table; do not re-derive it.

## What remains — two independent halves

### A. `effort` — unblocked and actionable NOW

Nothing external blocks this. Phase 5 declined it purely as a scope call: the phase body forbade threading `effort:` anywhere, on the strength of a negative this run overturned, and flipping a gated invariant across 15 call sites was not something to fold silently into a phase scoped as a recorded result.

1. **First, establish fidelity** — the one thing the run did NOT measure. It showed the request *ran* at `low`, not that `low` effort preserves mechanical transcription quality. Mechanical agents transcribe command output into schemas (`STAMP_ACK_SCHEMA`, `DIFF_SIGNALS_SCHEMA`, `ACK_SCHEMA`, `ESTIMATE_SCHEMA`); a degraded transcription is a silent data-corruption failure, not a visible one. Measure this before threading, not after.
2. Thread `effort: 'low'` at the 15 mechanical sites per the enumerated table, as a plain literal (never a module-level constant — the source text is byte-copied across files with different scopes).
3. Drop the `effort:` half of `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §2b **in the same commit**, so the repo never carries both the guard and the threading.
4. Re-measure per `mechanicalContextTrim.measurementProtocolForTheFollowUp` (`--since`-scoped so the pre-change corpus is not averaged in). Note the honest expectation: `effort` reduces *output/reasoning* tokens, not the per-agent context floor, so `floorByAgentClass` is the WRONG instrument for it — use the output-token columns. If nothing drops, revert rather than keeping it on faith.

### B. `agentType` — DONE except for a broader lane re-measure

Resolution is **confirmed** and the trim **measured** (2026-07-28, run `wf_40f5594e-208`, from a session rooted in the worktree so `.claude/agents/` was present at session start):

- Case B resolved with `toolNames: ["Bash", "StructuredOutput"]`; case C's registry listing now enumerates `rdm-mechanical`.
- Controlled pair, identical prompt, same session: **38689 → 29782 = −8907 tokens (−23.0 %)**, reproduced exactly by the E/F pair.
- Live `backlog` dispatch vs the pinned medians: `model:mechanical` 36877 → 29524 (−19.9 %), `fetch:report` 30098 → 24418 (−18.9 %). Both n=1 — directional, not a re-baseline.
- Scope item 3 is also answered: `agent(prompt, { schema })` returns correctly under the restricted `tools: Bash, StructuredOutput` list, and a per-call `model` still overrides the definition (the lane sidecar records `{"agentType":"rdm-mechanical","model":"haiku"}`).

**Correction worth carrying forward: the `claude -p` 2×2's 19894 (−42 %) overstates these call sites by 2.23×.** A Workflow subagent's default floor is far leaner than a CLI session's (38689 vs 47084) while the trimmed agent is slightly dearer (29782 vs 27190), so the margin roughly halves. Quote 8907/−23 % for the threaded sites.

What is left:

1. **Broaden the lane measurement.** Only `backlog` has been dispatched post-change, giving n=1 for `model` and `fetch` and nothing for the `gate`/`estimate`-class sites in `plan-review.js` and `estimate.js`. Dispatch those lanes and re-read `floorByAgentClass` with `--since` scoping, per `mechanicalContextTrim.measurementProtocolForTheFollowUp`, then record per-class n alongside the delta. Do **not** overwrite `preChangeMedianTokens`.
2. **Confirm `agentType` through `parallel()`** — `gather:*` in `document.js` and plan-review's per-phase fan-out both dispatch that way, and only sequential `agent()` calls have been exercised so far.
3. Note for whoever runs this: the definition must be present in the session's project root **at session start**. A session rooted outside this repo, or one that creates `.claude/agents/` mid-run, will not resolve it — that mistake produced the original invalid spike result.

### A note on the §2b guard's scope

`verify-workflow-review.sh` §2b's `agentType` guard greps only `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js`, deliberately. The local workflows are not covered because their definition lives in this same repo at the path the runtime searches, so a local `agentType` is resolvable in principle — it is unthreaded only pending step B1. Do not widen the guard to `$WF_DIR`; that would gate against the very change this task exists to make.

## Acceptance

- Half A: either the mechanical sites carry `effort: 'low'` with a recorded fidelity check and a measured output-token drop, or a recorded negative and no site edited. `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §2b's `effort:` guard is dropped in the same commit if and only if the sites were threaded.
- Half B: the spike is re-run from a session that can see the definition at session start; resolution is either confirmed (then `floorByAgentClass` is re-measured against the pinned pre-change medians and the delta recorded with its per-class n) or shown to fail, in which case the threading is reverted.
- Bidirectional harness assertions with planted-mutation self-tests in both directions for any option that does get threaded (mechanical sites carry it, judgment sites do not), plus a live completeness check derived from `.claude/workflows/*.js`. Hazard: the label regex is an unanchored substring match, so `act:` also matches the mechanical `act:round-note:` — isolate the judgment site with `act:'`. Same care for `estimate:rate:` vs `estimate:list`/`write`/`tier`.
- `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh`, `bash scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` all pass.

## Estimate

hard — Two independent halves spanning 15 byte-copied call sites across four workflows, a fidelity study whose failure mode is silent schema-transcription corruption, live multi-lane token re-measurement with per-class n, a gated harness invariant to flip with bidirectional planted-mutation self-tests, and revert-on-negative branches — cross-cutting and empirical, not a self-contained feature.

If nothing drops, revert rather than keeping it on faith.

Resolution is **confirmed** and the trim **measured** (2026-07-28, run `wf_40f5594e-208`, from a session rooted in the worktree so `.claude/agents/` was present at session start):

What is left:

1. **Broaden the lane measurement.** Only `backlog` has been dispatched post-change, giving n=1 for `model` and `fetch` and nothing for the `gate`/`estimate`-class sites in `plan-review.js` and `estimate.js`. `verify-workflow-review.sh` §2b's `agentType` guard greps only `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js`, deliberately. Do not widen the guard to `$WF_DIR`; that would gate against the very change this task exists to make.

**Corrected 2026-07-27 by phase 5's spike findings — the original framing of this task was wrong in two ways.**

1. The definition is named `rdm-mechanical.md`, not `mechanical.md`, and **no workflow script references it yet**. Phase 5 did NOT thread `agentType` into `autopilot.js` / `dispatch-phase.js` / `review-refute-fix.js`, so there is no dangling reference on the branch today.

This task previously reasoned by analogy from the `model` spike (an unknown `model` id resolves the agent to `null` rather than throwing) and concluded the degradation was "likely silent rather than loud". It is not. The Workflow runtime carries a dedicated raised error for `agentType`: `agent({agentType}): agent type '<X>' not found. Available agents: <list>`. `agentType` and `model` are handled by different code paths and only `model` has the silent-null hazard.

So the consequence of shipping an `agentType` reference without an emission surface is a **hard failure on first dispatch in every downstream repo**, not a degraded step in a lane that carries on. That is why phase 5 declined to create the reference and instead gated against one: `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §2b fails if any file under `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` mentions `agentType`, with a planted-mutation self-test.

**This task now gates a prerequisite, not a cleanup.** Until it lands, no distributed workflow template may reference an agent type. Landing it is what lifts the §2b guard.

**Updated 2026-07-27 — the raise is now OBSERVED. A previously recorded "new upstream blocker" here is RETRACTED.** Phase 5 dispatched `spike-agent-type.js` via the `Workflow` tool (run `wf_2bea58b9-38f`). Case C, which passes a deliberately unknown id, raised the not-found error, so item 2 above is confirmed by observation rather than by reading a runtime string table.

coherence.what_fails: The emitted workflows are byte copies of `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js`. `grep -c agentType` on all three returns 0, and §2b of `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` currently enforces that. (a) Weaken the check to a planted-fixture-only self-test and drop the floor — then the phase ships an inert definition with no live gate, which is a different deliverable from the one accepted. architectural-fit.location: Scope items 3(b), 4, 5 and Acceptance bullets 1-2
architectural-fit.what_fails: After this phase lands as written: `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` still contain zero `agentType` literals (verified by grep — every `agentType: 'rdm-mechanical'` in the repo lives in `backlog.js`, `document.js`, `estimate.js`, `plan-review.js`, `lib/plan-review.mjs`, or the spike). So the new reference-resolution check in `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` sweeps zero references. Scope 3(b) demands "an occurrence floor so it cannot pass vacuously, mirroring the existing shim-reference check" — the existing mirror is `[ "$SHIM_REF_COUNT" -ge 4 ]`; the analogous floor here can only be `>= 0`, which is exactly the vacuity the requirement forbids. Acceptance bullet 2, "the new resolution check fails when an `agentType` reference is corrupted", has nothing in a real emitted workflow to corrupt. Acceptance bullet 1 ("contains every agent definition its emitted workflows reference") passes vacuously over an empty reference set. The implementing agent is therefore forced either to write a knowingly vacuous gate or to silently expand scope into threading the distributed sites — and that expansion is itself blocked by two other gates the plan does not mention: `verify-workflow-review.sh` §2c pins `MECHANICAL_SITES` to the four local-only files and cross-checks a `THREADED` count against it (adding `agentType` to `autopilot.js` fails §2c(iii) unless the list is updated), and `verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` requires template/local byte-identity, so a template edit forces the matching local edit.

Removing the guard and adding the producer without ever creating a consumer leaves the repo with a shipped-but-unused file, a gate that cannot be made non-vacuous, and no remaining check that a future `agentType` reference in a template is safe — the exact regression §2b was protecting against. `docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md` shows the distributed workflows do have mechanical call sites (`model:mechanical`, `estimate:list`, `fetch:next` in `autopilot.js`; `fetch:phase-meta`, `stamp:in-progress`, `diff:signals` in `dispatch-phase.js`), so the consumer work is real, sizable, and currently unscoped.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Pick one and state it explicitly in the phase body. Either (a) fold the consumer into scope: thread `agentType: 'rdm-mechanical'` into the mechanical call sites of the three distributed workflows AND their byte-identical local copies, extend `MECHANICAL_SITES` in `verify-workflow-review.sh` §2c, and re-derive the §2c(iii) `MECH_EXPECTED`/`THREADED` counts — which makes the occurrence floor and the corruption self-test real; or (b) keep this phase producer-only and rewrite 3(b)/4 and acceptance bullet 2 to describe a forward-looking guard with no occurrence floor, explicitly deferring the floor to the phase that adds the first reference. If (b), also say what replaces §2b's protection in the interim, since the removal in scope item 5 leaves nothing checking that a template `agentType` value is emitted.

architectural-fit.concern: Scope omits updating the principles file, which states as fact that `.claude/agents/` is not distributed — the very claim this phase falsifies.
architectural-fit.location: Scope items 1-5 (no documentation step)

On merge, the principles file every subagent loads asserts the opposite of shipped behavior, and the next agent reading it will re-derive the retired constraint.
architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md is the loaded-into-every-subagent source of the constraint being lifted; leaving it stale is not cosmetic — it actively misinforms the agents that consume it, and CLAUDE.md itself designates this task as the authority for the lift.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Add a scope item: in the same commit as the emission surface and the §2b removal, rewrite CLAUDE.md's `.claude/agents/` section (heading, the "not distributed" sentence, and the `ship-mechanical-agent-type-downstream` lift pointer) and update the corresponding disposition rows in `docs/workflow-schemas.md`.

architectural-fit.concern: Acceptance verifies file presence only, while the failure mode the phase exists to prevent is a runtime raise that file presence does not rule out — CLAUDE.md's own watcher caveat says a scope's first `agents` file needs a session restart to resolve.
architectural-fit.location: Acceptance bullet 1 ("contains every agent definition its emitted workflows reference")
architectural-fit.what_fails: CLAUDE.md records: "Claude Code watches `.claude/agents/`, but the watcher covers only directories that existed at session start, so creating a scope's **first** agent file in a new `agents` directory needs a restart before it resolves." architectural-fit.why: This is the phase's central risk and the plan's acceptance criteria are blind to it by construction. It does not make the approach wrong, but the phase should not be able to report success while the shipped lane still hard-fails on first use.

restraint.concern: Scope item 2 prescribes a specific doctest/count edit that the plan's own chosen approach does not invalidate — an over-specified step that is a no-op at best and an incorrect edit at worst.
restraint.location: phase body, Scope item 2 ("Update the `generate_workflows().len() == 3` doctest and any sibling count assertions that the new surface invalidates")
restraint.what_fails: Scope item 1 specifies a *separate* emission surface (`generate_agents() -> Vec<AgentFile>`, its own `include_str!` template, wired alongside `write_workflows`). A separate surface cannot change `generate_workflows()`'s return length. Grepping the repo, the only `3`-valued assertions in this area are `rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs:348` (the doctest) and `:1252` (`generate_workflows_returns_three_files`), both scoped strictly to `generate_workflows`; `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` likewise pins `WORKFLOWS="autopilot.js dispatch-phase.js review-refute-fix.js"` as a workflow-only list, and the skills count stays 11. There are no sibling count assertions the new surface invalidates. Worse, `generate_workflows`'s own doc comment already states the opposite of the premise: "This is a separate emission surface from `generate_skills`/`SkillFile`... the two counts (skills vs. workflows) are independent and should not be summed when asserting either one." An implementing agent that treats a named scope item as work-to-be-done has two bad exits: edit a correct assertion to a wrong value, or fold the agent definition into `generate_workflows` (making 3 become 4) to satisfy the item — the latter contradicting scope item 1 and the doc comment's stated separation.
restraint.why: The plan spells out an implementation decision that should have been left to whoever carries it out. "Fix any assertions the new surface invalidates" is the risk-reducing instruction; naming a specific assertion that is not in fact invalidated converts a free-standing judgment call into a directive that points the wrong way.
restraint.recommendation: Drop the named doctest from scope item 2 and reduce it to the general form ("update any assertions the new surface invalidates — most likely none, since it is a separate surface"), or delete the item entirely and let the implementer's test run tell them. If keeping it, state explicitly that `generate_workflows().len() == 3` is expected to remain 3.

restraint.concern: Scope item 3(b) prescribes a specific anti-vacuity mechanism (an occurrence floor "mirroring the existing shim-reference check") for a check whose subject set is empty at landing time, so the copied mechanism cannot be satisfied as written.
restraint.location: phase body, Scope item 3(b) and Acceptance bullet 2
restraint.what_fails: `grep -rn agentType rdm-core/src/templates/` returns zero hits, and the three distributed workflows (`autopilot.js`, `dispatch-phase.js`, `review-refute-fix.js`) carry zero `agentType` literals — only the four local-only workflows (`backlog.js`, `estimate.js`, `document.js`, `plan-review.js`) do. Nothing in this phase's scope threads `agentType` into a distributed template (that is `finish-agent-type-effort-spike-and-thread-mechanical-sites`' subject, and the body itself frames this phase as "a prerequisite, not a cleanup"). So immediately after this phase lands, an emitted tree contains zero `agentType:` literals. A reference-resolution check with an occurrence floor over those literals — the mechanism the plan names — must either fail on a floor of >= 1 or be reduced to a floor of 0, which is exactly the vacuous pass the borrowed mechanism exists to prevent. The existing shim check it is modelled on works precisely because 4+ real `.claude/workflows/<name>.js` references exist to floor against (`verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` step 4, ">= 4" floor). Acceptance bullet 2 inherits the same problem: "fails when an `agentType` reference is corrupted" has no reference to corrupt.
restraint.why: This is over-specification by analogy: the plan copies a concrete mechanism from a sibling check without the precondition that made it work there. Stating the *property* (the check must not be able to pass vacuously) and leaving the mechanism to the implementer would have absorbed the empty-set case — a synthetic fixture workflow, or a planted reference in the self-test only — instead of prescribing a floor that cannot hold.
restraint.recommendation: Replace the prescribed occurrence floor with the property: "the resolution check must be provably non-vacuous — since the emission set carries no `agentType` literal yet, demonstrate it via the planted-corruption self-test (item 4) rather than an occurrence floor over real references." Alternatively, if a real floor is wanted, add an explicit scope item threading `agentType` into at least one distributed template in the same commit — but note that expands scope past 'prerequisite'.

restraint.concern: The body's retracted-history narrative and restated spike conclusions have grown past the point of reducing risk, and one non-actionable scope item (item 0, "recommended, not blocking") adds a step that cannot fail.
restraint.location: phase body, the two dated correction blocks and Scope item 0

Scope item 0 compounds this: a step explicitly marked "recommended, not blocking" has no failure mode, so it reads as a numbered obligation that carries none.

Consolidated from task `size-autopilot-nested-fetch-agent`.

Every autopilot-driven phase spends one **session-model (Opus)** subagent on `dispatch-phase`'s Stage-0 `fetch:phase-meta`. It is the only agent in a dispatch that carries no `model:` key, and on the autopilot-nested path there is nothing to hoist it away, so it runs at the most expensive tier available on every single phase.

Two independent causes stack, both landed and both on `main` as of `76317ff`:

1. **Phase 3's hoist never reaches a nested dispatch.** `.claude/workflows/autopilot.js`'s `realDeps.dispatch` builds the nested payload as `{ roadmap, phase, planOnly, maxPlanRevise?, maxCodeRework? }` and never sets `phaseMeta`, so `hoistedMetaComplete` (`.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js`) rejects and the fetch agent runs. This is expected, not a regression: `docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md`'s per-label replay table records `autopilot | fetch:phase-meta (nested dispatch) | 39 observed | 0 eliminated | 39 remaining | irreducible - autopilot cannot shell out`.

2. **When it does run it is deliberately unsized.** Stage-0 fetch is the one whitelisted bootstrap exemption in `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh`'s AC-MODEL sweep, because it is the agent that resolves the five per-step model ids (`plan`, `implement`, `review_find`, `review_verify`, `mechanical`). It cannot know its own tier before running, so it inherits the session model.

## Why "irreducible" is too strong

The inventory's `irreducible` verdict is correct about *hoisting* - a Workflow script cannot shell out, so autopilot genuinely cannot produce the payload itself without an agent. It does not follow that the agent must run at the session model. Autopilot already resolves `mechanicalModel` before the drive loop (hoisted from the caller as `cfg.mechanicalModel`, else `d.resolveMechanicalModel()`), and it fails closed on an empty result. That id is available on every iteration of the drive loop, including the first.

So autopilot can spawn the phase-meta fetch **itself**, at `mechanicalModel`, and pass the result down as `phaseMeta`. The chicken-and-egg that justifies the exemption inside `dispatch-phase` does not exist one level up, because autopilot has already broken it.

## Observed

Run `wf_133bc5a5-ce3` (autopilot on `workflow-token-reduction`, phase 4). Of 15 subagents spawned, exactly one has no `model` field in its sidecar meta - `agent-a4cebc645bdefce3b` - and its prompt is the `rdm phase show --roadmap workflow-token-reduction phase-4-per-class-context-floor --project rdm --format json` fetch. Every other agent carries an explicit `haiku`, `sonnet`, or `opus`.

## Candidate approaches

- **Autopilot pre-fetches.** Add a `d.fetchPhaseMeta(slug, stem, mechanicalModel)` dep that runs the same prompt as `buildFetchPrompt` at the mechanical tier, and forward the result as `payload.phaseMeta`. Converts an Opus step into a haiku step per phase and makes phase 3's hoist path live for the autonomous lane. Costs a byte-identical-copy edit in `lib/autopilot.mjs` + `autopilot.js`, plus the hand-maintained `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/autopilot.js` copy.
- **`dispatch-phase` accepts `mechanicalModel` as an arg.** Let a caller that already knows the id size Stage 0 directly, keeping the unsized path only for a truly cold direct `Workflow` invocation. Narrower change, and it also sizes the nested `stamp:in-progress` (20 observed, 0 eliminated on the same path).

Either way `hoistedMetaComplete` stays all-or-nothing and the unsized fallback must survive for a cold direct invocation.

## Acceptance

- On an autopilot-driven phase, no dispatch subagent runs without an explicit `model:`.
- A direct `Workflow` invocation of `dispatch-phase` with no hoisted args still works, still resolving models via the unsized bootstrap fetch.
- `docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md`'s `irreducible` rows for `fetch:phase-meta` (nested) and `stamp:in-progress` (nested) are corrected to distinguish "cannot be hoisted" from "cannot be sized", with the measured delta updated.
- `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh`'s AC-MODEL whitelist is narrowed to match whatever exemption actually remains, so it cannot pass vacuously.
- `scripts/verify-workflow-autopilot.sh` covers the new dep and its byte-identical-copy drift gate.

## Relation to the roadmap

Adjacent to `workflow-token-reduction` phase 5 (`trim-mechanical-agent-context`), which trims the context of mechanical agents that remain. This is a *tier* fix rather than a *context* fix, so it is separable - but the two touch the same call sites and phase 5 should not land a context trim that assumes this agent stays on the session model. Fold it into phase 5 or sequence it immediately after.

## Estimate

moderate — Well-scoped tier fix with a known mechanism, but it touches three byte-identical autopilot copies plus dispatch-phase arg threading, must preserve the cold-invocation unsized fallback, and requires corresponding doc corrections and updates to two verify harnesses (narrowing the AC-MODEL whitelist and adding drift-gate coverage).

coherence.concern: The plan's whole mechanism depends on autopilot's forwarded payload satisfying dispatch-phase's `hoistedMetaComplete`, which fails SILENTLY back to the exact unsized fetch being removed — and no acceptance criterion gates that contract.
coherence.location: Plan § Candidate approaches ("Autopilot pre-fetches") and § Acceptance criteria 1 and 5
coherence.what_fails: `hoistedMetaComplete` (.claude/workflows/lib/dispatch-phase.mjs:159-168) is all-or-nothing: it requires `body` non-empty, a non-empty `model` difficulty tier, and all five of `models.{plan,implement,review_find,review_verify,mechanical}`. On any miss, dispatch-phase.js:2098 logs 'no usable caller hoist' and runs the unsized `fetch:phase-meta` agent — a green run that costs exactly what the phase set out to save. The prompt and schema autopilot must reproduce (`buildFetchPrompt` at dispatch-phase.js:1832 and `PHASE_META_SCHEMA`) live in dispatch-phase.js's UNPROJECTED driver region, not in `lib/dispatch-phase.mjs`, so approach A duplicates them into a second workflow file with no generator and no drift gate. AC5 asks only for coverage of "the new dep and its byte-identical-copy drift gate", which is autopilot's own lib↔js copy and structurally cannot see this cross-file contract; AC1 ("no dispatch subagent runs without an explicit model:") is a runtime property that verify-workflow-autopilot.sh, which drives injected fakes, never observes.
coherence.why: An implementer can satisfy every stated acceptance criterion, land the change, and ship a no-op: one dropped or renamed key in autopilot's fetch result (or a later edit to dispatch-phase's required-key list) silently restores the Opus fetch with all harnesses passing. The plan itself notes hoistedMetaComplete stays all-or-nothing but never turns that hazard into a gate.
coherence.recommendation: Add an explicit acceptance criterion that a harness imports BOTH `lib/autopilot.mjs` and `lib/dispatch-phase.mjs` and asserts `hoistedMetaComplete(<autopilot's forwarded phaseMeta>, false) === true` for a representative fake fetch result, with a planted-mutation self-test (drop one of the five model ids / the tier and prove the assertion fails). Also state where the duplicated fetch prompt/schema lives and how it is kept from drifting from dispatch-phase's copy.

coherence.concern: Candidate approach B's secondary rationale and acceptance criterion 3 rest on a false premise: the nested `stamp:in-progress` agent is already sized at the mechanical tier.
coherence.location: Plan § Candidate approaches (second bullet) and § Acceptance criteria 3
coherence.what_fails: The plan says approach B "also sizes the nested `stamp:in-progress` (20 observed, 0 eliminated on the same path)", and AC3 asks that the `stamp:in-progress` (nested) inventory row be corrected "to distinguish 'cannot be hoisted' from 'cannot be sized'". But `.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:2183-2188` already passes `model: models.mechanical` on that agent — it runs after Stage 0 resolves the model map, so it has never been unsized. Passing a `mechanicalModel` arg into dispatch-phase would change its tier by exactly nothing. The inventory's main table (docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md:127) likewise already classifies it **redundant**, not irreducible; only the replay row at line 285 says "irreducible — same".
coherence.why: An implementer weighing the two approaches is told approach B buys a second saving that does not exist, which can drive the wrong choice; and AC3, followed literally, would replace one inaccurate doc row with a different inaccurate claim (that a mechanical-tier agent "cannot be sized"). The real open question for that row is elimination — autopilot cannot shell out, so it cannot truthfully set `alreadyInProgress` — which is a different axis entirely.
coherence.recommendation: Delete the "also sizes the nested `stamp:in-progress`" clause from approach B, and re-scope AC3 to the `fetch:phase-meta` (nested) row only, or restate the `stamp:in-progress` row correction in terms of elimination (`alreadyInProgress`) rather than sizing, noting it is already on the mechanical tier.

coherence.concern: Acceptance criterion 4 (narrow the AC-MODEL whitelist) is a no-op under the plan's own preserved-fallback constraint, and is achievable only under one of the two candidate approaches.
coherence.location: Plan § Acceptance criteria 4, read against "the unsized fallback must survive for a cold direct invocation"
coherence.what_fails: `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh:1355-1367` whitelists exactly one thing: an option block whose `label:` matches `fetch:(phase|task)-meta`. Both candidate approaches keep that call site verbatim as the cold-invocation fallback, so the "exemption that actually remains" is byte-for-byte the exemption already encoded — there is nothing to narrow under approach A. The sweep is also not vacuous today: it cross-checks extracted blocks against an independent call-site count (line 1350) and has two planted-mutation self-tests (lines 1370-1381).
coherence.why: An implementer who picks approach A (the plan's own preferred framing, since it is the one that makes phase 3's hoist path live) cannot satisfy AC4 as written and must either invent a cosmetic edit or silently skip a stated criterion. The AC's stated motive ("so it cannot pass vacuously") is also already met, so the criterion gives no signal about whether the fix worked.
coherence.recommendation: Either mark AC4 as approach-B-only, or restate it as something checkable under both: e.g. assert the whitelist matches exactly one label and that the whitelisted block is reachable only on the no-hoist branch, and add the positive assertion that autopilot's nested payload takes the hoisted branch (see the silent-fallback finding).

coherence.concern: The § Relation to the roadmap sequencing instruction is stale — the `workflow-token-reduction` phase 5 it tells the implementer to fold into or follow has already landed.
coherence.location: Plan § Relation to the roadmap
coherence.what_fails: `rdm phase list --roadmap workflow-token-reduction` reports phase 5 (`phase-5-trim-mechanical-agent-context`) as **done**, as are phases 1-7. "Fold it into phase 5 or sequence it immediately after" is therefore not an available choice, and the guard "phase 5 should not land a context trim that assumes this agent stays on the session model" is a constraint on work that already shipped. The § Why heading's "Phase 3's hoist" is likewise an unqualified cross-roadmap referent inside a document that is itself phase 3 of `regularize-mechanical-agents`.
coherence.why: Left as written, the implementer has to reverse-engineer whether the already-landed context trim baked in a session-model assumption at this call site — the plan raises the risk but, being stale, gives no instruction for the world as it now is.
coherence.recommendation: Replace the fold-or-sequence choice with the current fact (phase 5 landed) plus a concrete check: confirm whether the landed trim to the Stage-0 fetch prompt assumes the session model, and qualify "Phase 3's hoist" as `workflow-token-reduction` phase 3 so it is not read as this document.

coherence.concern: The § Observed evidence numbers do not match the cited run's sidecar, so the one measurement backing AC1 cannot be reproduced as stated.
coherence.location: Plan § Observed
coherence.what_fails: Run `wf_133bc5a5-ce3`'s subagent directory holds 79 `agent-*.meta.json` files, not 15, and THREE carry no `model` field: `agent-a43534b5c792c1657`, `agent-a4cebc645bdefce3b`, `agent-a7f5c8174e6185fc4`. All three are `fetch:phase-meta` prompts — for `phase-6-skip-non-gating-refutation`, `phase-4-per-class-context-floor`, and `phase-5-trim-mechanical-agent-context` respectively — one per dispatched phase, not one for the run.
coherence.why: The qualitative claim is not merely intact but stronger (the unsized fetch is the ONLY unsized agent class across 79 subagents, and it recurs once per phase rather than once per run), yet an implementer or reviewer re-deriving the numbers will find they disagree with the plan and may distrust the premise. It also understates the saving: the fix eliminates one Opus agent per phase, three in this run.
coherence.recommendation: Correct the counts to 79 subagents / three unsized, name all three agent ids and their phases, and state the saving per dispatched phase rather than per run.

architectural-fit.concern: Candidate approach 1 ("autopilot pre-fetches") requires duplicating the Stage-0 fetch prompt AND the PHASE_META contract into autopilot, but the plan proposes no single-source module and no cross-workflow drift gate — violating CLAUDE.md's stated convention that shared workflow logic is single-sourced in `.claude/workflows/lib/` and stamped into consumers behind a `--check` gate.
architectural-fit.location: Phase body § "Candidate approaches", first bullet ("Add a `d.fetchPhaseMeta(slug, stem, mechanicalModel)` dep that runs the same prompt as `buildFetchPrompt`") and § Acceptance, 5th bullet
architectural-fit.what_fails: `buildFetchPrompt` (.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:1832) and `PHASE_META_SCHEMA` (:1730) both sit OUTSIDE every generated/byte-copied region — they are above no `estimate-core` fence and below the `dispatch-outcome:end` marker at :1688, so they exist in exactly one authored place today. To emit a payload `hoistedMetaComplete` accepts, autopilot's new dep must reproduce the whole contract: non-empty `body`, a non-empty `model` difficulty tier, and all five model ids (`plan`, `implement`, `review_find`, `review_verify`, `mechanical`), each resolved with the exact `--tier`/no-`--tier` split the prompt encodes. Approach 1 copies that into `lib/autopilot.mjs` -> `autopilot.js` -> `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/autopilot.js`, giving four independently-authored copies of one contract. AC5 only asks that `verify-workflow-autopilot.sh` cover "the new dep and its byte-identical-copy drift gate" — that gate is autopilot-internal (lib vs js), and nothing gates autopilot's copy against dispatch-phase's canonical one. When dispatch-phase's schema later changes (e.g. a sixth resolved step — sibling phase 6 in this same roadmap threads `findModel`/`verifyModel` into another call site), autopilot keeps emitting the old shape, `hoistedMetaComplete` rejects it all-or-nothing, and dispatch-phase silently falls back to the unsized session-model fetch. Both harnesses stay green, the run now pays for TWO fetches instead of one, and this phase's own AC1 regresses with no signal.
architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md states the constraint directly: "The Workflow runtime cannot import/require ... Shared pipeline logic is therefore kept single-source in `.claude/workflows/lib/` and stamped verbatim into consumers by `scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh` (run it after editing a lib/*.mjs; `--check` mode gates drift)." Every existing cross-workflow sharing in this repo honors that — `review.mjs` via gen-workflow-review.sh, `estimate-core` via gen-workflow-estimate.sh into all three consumers including autopilot.js. Approach 1 as written is the first cross-workflow logic copy with no generator and no `--check`, and it fails soft (silent fallback) rather than loud, which is the failure mode the drift gates exist to prevent.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Make the AC set gate the duplication, not just autopilot's internal copy. Either (a) commit to approach 2, which threads a model id rather than a prompt and duplicates no contract; or (b) if approach 1 is chosen, require that `buildFetchPrompt` + `PHASE_META_SCHEMA` move into a lib module stamped into BOTH `dispatch-phase.js` and `autopilot.js` by a generator with a `--check` mode (the `estimate-core` three-consumer stamp is the exact precedent), and add an AC that a planted divergence between the two copies fails a harness.

architectural-fit.concern: AC4 (narrow the AC-MODEL whitelist so it cannot pass vacuously) cannot be satisfied by approach 1, which the plan's "Either way" framing presents as independently sufficient.
architectural-fit.location: Phase body § Acceptance, 4th bullet, read against § "Candidate approaches" first bullet and the closing "Either way ..." sentence
architectural-fit.what_fails: Approach 1 leaves `dispatch-phase.js` byte-unchanged by construction — the driver's `else` branch at :2098-2112 still spawns `agent(buildFetchPrompt(...), { label: 'fetch:phase-meta', ... })` with no `model:` key, and AC2 explicitly requires that cold path to keep working. `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh`'s sweep whitelists by label (`if ($0 ~ /label: .fetch:(phase|task)-meta./) next`, :1360), so with the call site unchanged there is nothing to narrow: the exemption still covers exactly one still-unsized call. An implementer who picks approach 1 will reach AC4 with no way to satisfy it and will either skip it or weaken it cosmetically. Approach 2 does have a path — `model: mechanicalModel || undefined` on that call site, since the sweep only tests for the literal `model:` key and dispatch-phase.js:1036 already records that `model: undefined` is inert — which would let the whitelist be dropped outright while AC2's cold invocation still works.
architectural-fit.why: The plan's own ACs are the implementing agent's gate. Presenting two approaches as interchangeable ("Either way `hoistedMetaComplete` stays all-or-nothing") when only one can satisfy AC4 pushes the decision to an agent that will discover the conflict mid-implementation.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Drop the "Either way" framing and state that AC4 requires the sizing to reach dispatch-phase's own call site — i.e. approach 2, or approach 1 plus the `model: mechanicalModel || undefined` threading. Name the `model: undefined` inertness precedent (dispatch-phase.js:1036) so the implementer knows the cold-invocation fallback survives it.

architectural-fit.concern: The plan asserts approach 2 "also sizes the nested `stamp:in-progress`" and AC3 asks to correct that inventory row for sizing — but `stamp:in-progress` is already explicitly sized and harness-gated.
architectural-fit.location: Phase body § "Candidate approaches", second bullet ("it also sizes the nested `stamp:in-progress` (20 observed, 0 eliminated on the same path)") and § Acceptance, 3rd bullet
architectural-fit.what_fails: `.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:2183-2188` spawns `stamp:in-progress` with `model: models.mechanical`, and `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh`'s AC-MECHANICAL-TIER section asserts exactly that (`assert_label_model "$TMP/agent-blocks" 'stamp:in-progress' 'models.mechanical'`) with a planted-repoint self-test. The `irreducible` verdict on `docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md:285` sits in a per-label replay table whose columns are observed / eliminated / remaining — it is a claim about ELIMINATION (hoisting), not about tier. So there is no sizing defect on that agent for approach 2 to fix, and AC3's "cannot be sized" correction has no referent on the `stamp:in-progress` row. The plan's own § Observed section corroborates this: of 15 subagents in run `wf_133bc5a5-ce3`, exactly ONE lacked a `model` field, and it was the fetch — the stamp carried one.
architectural-fit.why: This is the stated tie-breaker favoring approach 2 ("Narrower change, AND it also sizes..."). An implementer taking it at face value will either pick approach 2 for a benefit that does not exist, or spend effort re-threading a model id onto an agent that already has one and is already gated.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Strike the sizing claim from the approach-2 bullet. Narrow AC3 to the `fetch:phase-meta` (nested) row only, and if the `stamp:in-progress` (nested) row is still worth touching, say plainly that it remains irreducible for ELIMINATION on the nested path and is already correctly sized at `models.mechanical`.

architectural-fit.concern: Approach 2's "dispatch-phase arg threading" lands inside the byte-copied `dispatch-outcome` region, so its true cost is three more synchronized copies plus an existing drift gate — none of which the Estimate or AC5 enumerates.
architectural-fit.location: Phase body § "Candidate approaches" second bullet and § Estimate ("three byte-identical autopilot copies plus dispatch-phase arg threading")
architectural-fit.what_fails: `parseDispatchArgs` — the function that would gain a `mechanicalModel` field — is at `.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:1214`, inside the `>>> dispatch-outcome:begin <<<` / `:end` fence spanning :1155-:1688. `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh` section 2 gates that region byte-for-byte against `.claude/workflows/lib/dispatch-phase.mjs`. So approach 2 costs an edit to lib/dispatch-phase.mjs, the identical edit to dispatch-phase.js, the same again in `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/dispatch-phase.js` (byte-gated by verify-agent-config-distribution.sh), and it must keep the section-2 drift gate green. AC5 names only `scripts/verify-workflow-autopilot.sh`, and the Estimate's "moderate" rating counts only the autopilot copies.
architectural-fit.why: Understating which byte-gated regions a change touches is how a workflow edit lands green in one harness and red in another. The repo's convention is that every such region has a named drift gate; the plan should name the ones it will trip.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Add `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh` (section 2 block drift) and `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` to AC5's harness list if approach 2 is taken, and note in the Estimate that `parseDispatchArgs` is inside the byte-copied `dispatch-outcome` block so the lib copy must be edited first.

restraint.concern: The acceptance criteria quietly pre-commit to one of the two approaches the plan deliberately leaves open, over-specifying the mechanism instead of the outcome.
restraint.location: phase-3-size-autopilot-nested-fetch-agent, "## Acceptance" bullet 5 ("scripts/verify-workflow-autopilot.sh covers the new dep and its byte-identical-copy drift gate"), read against "## Candidate approaches" and its closing "Either way ..." sentence
restraint.what_fails: The body presents two genuinely different mechanisms and explicitly declines to pick ("Either way `hoistedMetaComplete` stays all-or-nothing..."), which is the restrained choice. AC5 then closes the choice: "the new dep" and autopilot-side drift coverage only exist under approach A (add `d.fetchPhaseMeta(...)` to `lib/autopilot.mjs`). Approach B — `dispatch-phase` accepts `mechanicalModel` as an arg — adds no dep to autopilot at all: `.claude/workflows/autopilot.js:1033-1042` shows `dispatch: async function (slug, stem, planOnly, budgets)` building `payload = { roadmap, phase, planOnly }` plus two optional budgets, so B is a one-key payload/signature thread, and the harness that would need new coverage is `scripts/verify-workflow-dispatch.sh` (where the AC-MODEL whitelist at lines 1312-1381 and the hoist simulation at 1823-1997 already live), not `verify-workflow-autopilot.sh`. restraint.recommendation: Restate AC5 mechanism-neutrally, e.g. "whichever harness covers the changed surface (`verify-workflow-autopilot.sh` for an autopilot-side dep, `verify-workflow-dispatch.sh` for a dispatch-phase arg) gains coverage for the new path and its byte-identical-copy drift gate."
