## Context

When a lane agent stalls or its work is reworked, the lane re-dispatches but does not tell
the new agent that prior work exists. Two independent gaps, one in a prompt and one in
documentation. Neither needs new persistence — the durable state is already on disk.

**What already reuses correctly** (do not "fix" these):

- `rdm worktree add` is idempotent — it prints the existing path and `(existing worktree —
  nothing to create)`. The durable-state layer is sound.
- `plan:revise` receives the prior plan document plus the findings; the plan is never
  re-authored within a run.
- `implement:rework` receives the phase body, the approved plan, the ranked findings, AND
  the unmet acceptance-criteria rows as a deliberately separate channel.

**Gap 1 — the implement prompt asserts there is nothing to reuse.**
`buildImplementPrompt` opens with "You are an implementation agent. You are seeded with ONLY
the item body and the approved plan below." On a rework pass that is false — findings and AC
gaps are appended below it — and, more expensively, it never mentions that the worktree
already holds the prior attempt's commits. The prompt asks for `git diff main...HEAD` only at
the END, to produce the `IMPLEMENT_RESULT` diff report, never at the start to orient. The
code-review prompt already does this correctly ("Inspect the implementation diff (use git log
/ git diff in the worktree)"); the implement prompt simply never learned it.

This also reaches the layer we do NOT control. Stalled-agent retries are owned by the
Workflow runtime: it re-dispatches on a silent model stream with a fresh `agentId` and a new
transcript, and there is no hook in lane code (a grep of the workflow libs finds only
semantic retries — `maxCodeRework`, `maxPlanRevise`, `parkWithRetry`, advance attempts).
Because the runtime re-sends the SAME prompt, fixing the orientation defect makes stall
recovery cheaper for free — and it matters most exactly there, since a stalled implement
agent may have committed before dying, so its work is on disk and the retry is the agent most
likely to redo or conflict with it.

script, in the `rdm-autopilot` / `rdm-dispatch-phase` skill shims, or in

directly: autopilot run `wf_974e3812-817` died mid-flight against this repo's own
`workflow-token-reduction` roadmap having spent ~3.2M subagent tokens, and its journal records
**41 `started` and 32 `result` entries** — so 32 completed agents had cached results available
and only the 9 API-failed agents lacked them. The review was nonetheless re-run from scratch.

   restart — explicitly covering both the rework case and the case where a previous attempt

   `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/dispatch-phase.js`. Note `buildImplementPrompt` is NOT in

3. Preserve the existing END-of-prompt diff-report instructions byte-for-byte in wording that
   `deriveSignals` depends on (same three-dot `main...HEAD` base, same 40000-character

- Making orphaned stall attempts visible to the measurement harness — owned by task
  `lane-retry-attempt-token-waste`, which is deliberately still open.

- [ ] No plan-persistence mechanism is added, and the deferral is recorded pointing at `autopilot-run-accounting/phase-3-run-artifact`.

coherence.concern: Step 1's orientation instruction ("read what is already committed and build on it rather than restart") does not distinguish a prior attempt at THIS phase from earlier phases of the same roadmap that are already on the shared branch — the dominant case in this lane.
coherence.location: Steps §1 / AC1; .claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:1935 buildImplementPrompt, and the diff-base comment at :1988-1995
coherence.what_fails: dispatch-phase implements every phase of a roadmap in ONE shared per-roadmap worktree. The code already documents this at the `buildDiffSignalsPrompt` comment: "For a phase implemented in the SHARED per-roadmap worktree, earlier phases of the same roadmap are already on the branch, so a later phase sees the whole branch diff." So on a first-pass dispatch of phase 5, `git log main..HEAD` / `git diff main...HEAD` return phases 1-4's commits — not a prior attempt at phase 5. A prompt that says "prior work exists in this worktree, build on it rather than restart" therefore hands a fresh implementer a large, wholly unrelated diff and invites the exact failure the phase is trying to prevent in reverse: concluding the work is already partly done and under-implementing, or attributing someone else's phase to its own approved plan.
coherence.why: The plan's stated goal is cheaper/safer reuse of prior work; a prompt that conflates sibling-phase commits with this phase's own prior attempt degrades first-pass quality (the common case) to buy a rework/stall-path saving (the rare case). The plan's framing text only ever discusses the rework case and the died-partway case, so an implementer following it as written has no cue to handle the shared-branch case.
coherence.recommendation: Have step 1 require the orientation paragraph to state the shared-worktree semantics explicitly: the branch may already carry commits from EARLIER phases of the same roadmap (which are context, not this phase's work) as well as a prior attempt at this item; instruct the agent to scope by the approved plan's own scope and to treat pre-existing commits as ground truth to build on, not as evidence its own item is done. target:
phase regularize-mechanical-agents/phase-5-record-review-non-participation

## Context

When a dimension finder dies on an API error, the canonical review pipeline drops it and
reports a normal result. There is no retry, and nothing in the returned OUTCOME records that
the dimension did not participate. A review that ran 3 of 7 dimensions is indistinguishable
from one that ran all 7 and found little.

This is a correctness gap, not a cost one. It is also inconsistent with the rest of this
repo, which plants mutation self-tests specifically to prove gates are not vacuous.

All line references are to `.claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs` on `main` at the time of
writing; re-confirm them before editing.

### Three distinct defects, in increasing severity

**1. Partial failure is silently tolerated.** `:1150-1160` throws only when EVERY dimension
returns null ("One dimension dropping to null is tolerated resilience"). `:1166`
(`perDimension.filter(Boolean).flat().filter(Boolean)`) then filters the nulls away. Observed:
autopilot run `wf_974e3812-817` dropped four finder dimensions to API 500/529 errors
(`pipeline[0]`, `[1]`, `[3]`, `[6]` — `ac`, `correctness`, `architecture`, `security`) and its
review reported a normal result. Note two of those are always-on dimensions.

**2. A dead `ac` finder reads as a clean acceptance-criteria table.** `acTable` initialises to
`null` (`:1083`) and is assigned only on success (`:1107-1109`, guarded by
`found && Array.isArray(found.ac)`). `acTableHasGap` (`:906`) does
`const list = Array.isArray(acTable) ? acTable : []` and then `list.some(...)`, so
`acTableHasGap(null) === false`. `classifyOutcome` (`:1027`) consults it as one of its two
outcome channels. Therefore an `ac` finder that dies produces no AC table, the AC channel
contributes nothing, and — absent an unrelated blocking finding — the outcome is `reviewed`.
The dimension that owns the acceptance-criteria contract can fail to run and yield a clean
verdict. `dispatch-phase.js` already has a branch for "an AC-only gap can force `rework` with
an EMPTY survivors array", so the AC channel was reasoned about carefully; the table being
ABSENT versus CLEAN was not.

**3. Both guards are inert in plan mode.** The null-to-throw conversion (`:1101`) and the
all-null guard (`:1155`) are each conditioned on `findModel &&`.
`.claude/workflows/lib/plan-review.mjs` calls `runPlanReview({ target: ... })` at `:688` and
`:713` passing NO `findModel`/`verifyModel` (deliberately — see the sibling task
`thread-plan-review-judgment-models`, which is a separate concern). So in plan mode `findModel`
is undefined, neither guard can fire, and a null finder flows through `(null && …) || []` as an
empty finding list. Every plan dimension could die, `classifyPlanOutcome([])` would yield
`reviewed`, and `GATE_POLICY.plan` would then CLEAR the `needs-plan-review` tag on the strength
of a review that never ran. This is the worst of the three and must not be fixed by merely
threading models — the guards should not depend on whether a model was passed.

### Why retry is the right lever, and transcript-resume is not

`agent()` returns `null` only AFTER the runtime has exhausted its own internal retries, so a
second-order retry from lane code is the first retry we control. Finders and refuters are
read-only and idempotent, so re-dispatching one is safe.

**Transcript-resume was considered and rejected. Do not revisit it in this phase.** `agent()`
accepts a prompt and opts; there is no resume-a-conversation parameter, and the runtime's stall
retry re-dispatches the prompt rather than replaying a transcript. "Resuming" would mean
reading `agent-<id>.jsonl` and synthesising a new prompt embedding a digest of prior turns —
re-seeding, not resuming. The cost math opposes it for exactly the agents that die: measured
stalled attempts ran 544,878 / 41,566 / 41,365 tokens (task `lane-retry-attempt-token-waste`)
while a finder's entire product is a small JSON verdict, so feeding a large transcript back
costs more than re-running the finder. The one agent whose prior work is both expensive and
durable is `implement`, and its work is already committed in the worktree — git is the better
resume point, which is phase 4's concern, not this one.

**A `null` cannot be attributed to a cause.** It means either a transient API death after
retries or an unknown/unavailable model id (the `model` spike's silent-null consequence).
Nothing distinguishes them at the call site. Retrying once handles both acceptably: a transient
failure usually succeeds on the retry, and a misconfigured model fails twice and is then
recorded loudly as non-participation. Do not attempt to classify the cause.

## Steps

1. In `buildReviewPipeline`, retry a finder that resolves to null/undefined **once** before
   treating it as non-participation. Bound it at one extra attempt (no exponential backoff, no
   loop) and make the retry unconditional on `findModel`.
2. Track per-dimension participation and return it: extend the pipeline's return value from
   `{ survivors, acTable }` to also carry which dimensions ran and which failed after retry.
   Keep the existing keys' meanings unchanged so current consumers keep working.
3. Distinguish an ABSENT AC table from a clean one. Either represent "the `ac` dimension did
   not run" explicitly rather than leaving `acTable === null` to mean both, or have
   `classifyOutcome` consult participation alongside `acTableHasGap`. Do not silently widen
   `acTableHasGap` itself — its current contract (a table with no FAIL/PARTIAL rows has no gap)
   is correct for a table that exists.
4. Make both existing guards independent of `findModel` so plan mode is covered. Preserve the
   distinct loud failure for the wholesale-misconfiguration case; its message names the
   `[models]` bindings and should stay recognisable.
5. **Gating policy — DECIDED: note it, do not block.** A non-participating dimension is
   recorded, never gated on. It does not force `rework`, does not force `escalated`, and does
   not hold back the plan gate — `needs-plan-review` still clears on an otherwise-`reviewed`
   plan review. Rationale: a transient API blip must not stall the autonomous lane, and the
   record makes the reduced coverage auditable after the fact. Do NOT add a gating branch for
   it in either mode.

   The consequence this accepts, stated plainly so it is not rediscovered as a bug: an
   incomplete review can still yield `reviewed`, and a phase can land via `rdm-land` with an
   always-on dimension never having run. That is the deliberate trade. It is only tolerable if
   the note is actually visible, which is what step 5b exists for.

5b. **Surface the note where a human will see it — a structured field alone is not enough.**
   Include non-participation in the OUTCOME's `summary` text, not just as a machine-readable
   key, so it reaches the places summaries already flow: the review report, the recorded
   status/reason, and the run log. A dimension that silently failed and is then silently
   recorded is no better than today.
6. Thread participation into the OUTCOME so a caller can see it, and update the canonical
   OUTCOME contract in `docs/workflow-schemas.md` in the same commit.
7. Add the missing spec prose. § Filter & consolidate already states that a crashing REFUTER
   is kept un-refuted rather than dropped; there is no counterpart for a crashing FINDER. Add
   one in the `//|` region. Remember this region is rendered into the shipped skill templates
   by `scripts/gen-skill-review.sh` in BOTH `--mode code` and `--mode plan`, so tag the lines
   correctly (`//|` shared vs `//|code|` / `//|plan|`) and check the rendered output in both.
8. Restamp the consumers with `scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh` (`review-refute-fix.js`,
   `dispatch-phase.js`, `plan-review.js`) — this is a stamped change, so the generator, not a
   hand edit, must produce the copies.

## Non-goals

- Threading `findModel`/`verifyModel` into `plan-review.js` — owned by phase 6 of this
  roadmap (`phase-6-thread-plan-review-judgment-models`). This phase must make the guards work
  WITHOUT models being passed, so the two are independent and neither blocks the other. Order
  them either way; if phase 6 lands first, this phase's `findModel`-independence requirement
  still stands, because a caller may always omit the models.
- Building transcript-resume or plan persistence (see above, and phase 4's non-goals).
- Making orphaned stall attempts visible to the measurement harness — task
  `lane-retry-attempt-token-waste`.
- Changing the runtime's own internal retry behaviour, which is not reachable from lane code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A finder resolving to null is retried exactly once before being recorded as non-participation, and the retry does not depend on whether a model was passed.
- [ ] A dimension that failed after retry is reported in the pipeline's return value and in the OUTCOME; a caller can tell 3-of-7 coverage from 7-of-7.
- [ ] A dead `ac` finder is distinguishable from a table with no FAIL/PARTIAL rows, and the distinction is recorded and surfaced. Per the decided policy it does NOT change the outcome — a review missing its `ac` dimension may still be `reviewed`, but must never look complete.
- [ ] With NO models passed (plan mode's real configuration), a single dead finder is recorded and every dead finder still fails loudly — verified by a test that passes no `findModel`.
- [ ] A plan review with a non-participating dimension still clears `needs-plan-review` (per the decided policy), and the non-participation is recorded in its OUTCOME and summary.
- [ ] No gating branch is introduced for non-participation in either mode; a test asserts a review with a dead dimension yields the same outcome it would have without the feature, differing only in the recorded coverage and summary.
- [ ] § Filter & consolidate states the finder-crash rule, rendered correctly in both `--mode code` and `--mode plan` skill outputs.
- [ ] `scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh --check` and `scripts/gen-skill-review.sh --check` pass in both modes; consumers were restamped by the generator, not by hand.
- [ ] `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` passes, with planted-mutation self-tests proving the retry, the participation record, and the absent-AC-table branch each actually fire.
- [ ] `docs/workflow-schemas.md`'s OUTCOME contract reflects the new field, in the same commit.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` entry in the same commit, since skill and workflow template bytes are what `agent-config` emits.

## Estimate

hard — Changes the semantics of the canonical review pipeline's outcome classification (retry, participation tracking, absent-vs-clean AC table, model-independent guards) and ripples through both mode renderings of the spec prose, three generator-stamped consumers, the OUTCOME contract docs, and new planted-mutation harness self-tests — cross-cutting and gate-critical.

phase workflow-token-reduction/4

## Context

Phase 3 removes the mechanical agents that can be eliminated outright. Some cannot: a call site with no caller to hoist to and no adjacent agent to absorb it is irreducible, and phase 3's classification table names that set. This phase trims what those remaining agents cost per invocation.

Given a ~36.8k-token intercept per agent before any work is done, per-agent context is the whole cost of a mechanical agent. Two Workflow-runtime options address it and **neither is used anywhere** under `.claude/workflows/`:

- `opts.agentType` — resolves against the same registry as the Agent tool, so a purpose-built agent definition can carry a trimmed system prompt and a restricted tool list. A mechanical fetch agent needs Bash and `StructuredOutput`; it does not need Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, Artifact, or Task, and every unused tool's schema is paid for on every agent.
- `opts.effort` — `'low'` is appropriate here and only here. These agents make no judgment call; they run a command and transcribe its output. This is deliberately **not** applied to finders or refuters, whose task is exactly the judgment that low effort degrades.

### This phase is feasibility-gated

Neither `agentType` nor `effort:` appears anywhere under `.claude/workflows/` today, so this is a greenfield spike against runtime capability this project has never exercised. Two questions are open and must be answered **first**, because the answers determine whether there is a change to make at all:

1. Is the `agentType` registry reachable from the Workflow runtime, and does a custom agent definition actually resolve there?
2. Is the project `CLAUDE.md` (~11.7k tokens) loaded into a custom `agentType` subagent, and how much does that move the floor?

A recorded negative result is a **legitimate completion of this phase**, on the same terms the refuter-model-tiering phase grants itself: if the registry is unreachable, or if `CLAUDE.md` loads unavoidably and the remaining trim is not worth the maintenance surface, the phase lands the measurement and the written finding and stops. It does not restructure `CLAUDE.md` speculatively, and it does not leave phase 3's completed elimination work stranded — that work has already landed independently.

### Distribution surface

The same constraint phase 3 operates under applies here. `autopilot.js`, `dispatch-phase.js` and `review-refute-fix.js` have hand-maintained byte-identical copies under `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` embedded by `rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs` via `include_str!`, and **no generator writes them**. Any workflow `.js` edited here must be re-synced by hand or `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` hard-fail, and CI runs every `scripts/verify-*.sh`.

## Steps

1. **Feasibility check, before any implementation.** Follow whatever registry mechanism `agentType` resolves against and confirm it is reachable from the Workflow runtime. Record the answer. If it is not reachable, record that finding, skip to step 7, and complete the phase on the negative result.
2. Determine empirically whether the project `CLAUDE.md` is loaded into a custom `agentType` subagent, and by how much it moves the per-agent floor. If it is unavoidable, record that as a finding and stop pursuing it — do not restructure `CLAUDE.md` speculatively. Fold the measured floor into the step 6 decision about whether the change is worth keeping.
3. Define a mechanical subagent type with a minimal system prompt and the smallest tool set that still lets it run a command and return structured output, for the call sites phase 3 classified irreducible.
4. Thread `agentType` and `effort: 'low'` through those remaining mechanical `agent()` call sites, honouring each call site's maintenance route from phase 3's table: keep a lib the single source and re-run its generator where the site is stamped, and edit both halves of a byte-identical copied driver region where it is not.
5. Verify no judgment agent is touched: finders, refuters, planners, implementers and the plan-review `act` step keep their current model and default effort. `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §5b-mechanical already asserts `act:*` must not be pinned — that assertion must still pass unchanged.
6. Re-sync `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` from `.claude/workflows/` for every one of those files this phase touched, and run `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` to confirm byte-identity is restored.
7. Re-run `scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs` over a fresh dispatch and compare the mechanical-class per-agent floor against `docs/token-baseline.json`. Record the delta, or the negative result from step 1 or 2.
8. Extend the relevant `verify-workflow-*.sh` harnesses to assert that remaining mechanical call sites carry the new options and that judgment call sites do not, with planted-mutation self-tests in both directions. If the phase completed on a negative result, this step is not applicable and the finding stands in its place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Whether the `agentType` registry is reachable from the Workflow runtime is answered explicitly and written down, before any call site is edited.
- [ ] Whether `CLAUDE.md` loads into a custom `agentType` subagent is answered empirically and written down, with its effect on the per-agent floor quantified.
- [ ] **If step 1 establishes the registry is reachable:** every mechanical `agent()` call site that remains after phase 3 passes the mechanical `agentType` and `effort: 'low'`; no judgment call site does. **If it is not reachable**, this criterion is satisfied instead by the recorded negative result and no call site is edited.
- [ ] The measured per-agent floor for the mechanical class drops against `docs/token-baseline.json`, and the delta is recorded. If it does not drop, the negative result is recorded and the change is reverted rather than kept on faith.
- [ ] `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §5b-mechanical passes unchanged, including its assertion that `act:*` is not pinned.
- [ ] Any workflow `.js` this phase edited is byte-identical to its `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` copy, and `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` both pass. Vacuously satisfied if no `.js` was edited.
- [ ] If call sites were edited, a harness asserts in both directions which of them carry the new options, with planted-mutation self-tests proving the assertions are not vacuous.
- [ ] Lane behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the same outcomes are produced for the same inputs.

## Estimate

hard — A greenfield feasibility spike against never-exercised Workflow runtime capability (agentType registry, CLAUDE.md loading) whose outcome is genuinely uncertain, layered on cross-cutting edits to multiple workflow scripts plus hand-maintained byte-identical template copies, token re-measurement against the baseline, and bidirectional planted-mutation harness assertions.

Any workflow `.js` edited here must be re-synced by hand or `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` hard-fail, and CI runs every `scripts/verify-*.sh`.

## Steps

1. **Feasibility check, before any implementation.** Follow whatever registry mechanism `agentType` resolves against and confirm it is reachable from the Workflow runtime. Record the answer. If it is not reachable, record that finding, skip to step 7, and complete the phase on the negative result.
2. Determine empirically whether the project `CLAUDE.md` is loaded into a custom `agentType` subagent, and by how much it moves the per-agent floor. If it is unavoidable, record that as a finding and stop pursuing it — do not restructure `CLAUDE.md` speculatively. Fold the measured floor into the step 6 decision about whether the change is worth keeping.
3. Define a mechanical subagent type with a minimal system prompt and the smallest tool set that still lets it run a command and return structured output, for the call sites phase 3 classified irreducible.
4. Thread `agentType` and `effort: 'low'` through those remaining mechanical `agent()` call sites, honouring each call site's maintenance route from phase 3's table: keep a lib the single source and re-run its generator where the site is stamped, and edit both halves of a byte-identical copied driver region where it is not.
5. Verify no judgment agent is touched: finders, refuters, planners, implementers and the plan-review `act` step keep their current model and default effort. `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §5b-mechanical already asserts `act:*` must not be pinned — that assertion must still pass unchanged.
6. Re-sync `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` from `.claude/workflows/` for every one of those files this phase touched, and run `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` to confirm byte-identity is restored.
7. Re-run `scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs` over a fresh dispatch and compare the mechanical-class per-agent floor against `docs/token-baseline.json`. Record the delta, or the negative result from step 1 or 2.
8. Extend the relevant `verify-workflow-*.sh` harnesses to assert that remaining mechanical call sites carry the new options and that judgment call sites do not, with planted-mutation self-tests in both directions. If the phase completed on a negative result, this step is not applicable and the finding stands in its place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Whether the `agentType` registry is reachable from the Workflow runtime is answered explicitly and written down, before any call site is edited.
- [ ] Whether `CLAUDE.md` loads into a custom `agentType` subagent is answered empirically and written down, with its effect on the per-agent floor quantified.
- [ ] **If step 1 establishes the registry is reachable:** every mechanical `agent()` call site that remains after phase 3 passes the mechanical `agentType` and `effort: 'low'`; no judgment call site does. **If it is not reachable**, this criterion is satisfied instead by the recorded negative result and no call site is edited.
- [ ] The measured per-agent floor for the mechanical class drops against `docs/token-baseline.json`, and the delta is recorded. If it does not drop, the negative result is recorded and the change is reverted rather than kept on faith.
- [ ] `scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh` §5b-mechanical passes unchanged, including its assertion that `act:*` is not pinned.
- [ ] Any workflow `.js` this phase edited is byte-identical to its `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` copy, and `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` both pass. Vacuously satisfied if no `.js` was edited.
- [ ] If call sites were edited, a harness asserts in both directions which of them carry the new options, with planted-mutation self-tests proving the assertions are not vacuous.
- [ ] Lane behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the same outcomes are produced for the same inputs.

## Estimate

target:
phase workflow-token-reduction/workflow-token-reduction

Cut token consumption in the `.claude/workflows/` autonomous lane, measuring every change against a committed baseline rather than against intuition.

## Why

A survey of the 20 lane runs on disk (autopilot / dispatch-phase / plan-review / backlog / estimate) found spend concentrated in review, not implementation:

| class | agents | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| review — find | 366 | 37% |
| review — refute | 492 | 36% |
| mechanical (fetch/stamp/estimate/diff) | 191 | 11% |
| implement | 37 | 8% |
| plan author/revise | 53 | 6% |

Review outweighs implementation ~8.6:1. A linear fit of tokens against tool calls gives an intercept of ~36.8k tokens per agent before any work is done, and the cheapest agent observed cost 27k — so a large fraction of lane spend is per-agent context loading, repeated across 1,156 agents. `CLAUDE.md` (~11.7k tokens) plus the user-global one (~3.3k) is loaded into every one of them, including agents whose entire job is running a single `rdm` command.

## Measurement caveat this roadmap must fix first

Those figures come from `workflowProgress[].tokens` and `totalTokens` in the session sidecars. The sibling `autopilot-run-accounting` roadmap establishes from a measured run that those fields are **not a cost basis**: they do not reconcile with deduped per-class totals and omit cache reads entirely (36.7M cache reads in a run whose non-cache-read classes summed to 4.4M). The class *ranking* above is believed sound; the absolute totals understate traffic and are blind to any change that trades cache-write for cache-read.

Phase 1 therefore re-derives the baseline from the `agent-*.jsonl` transcripts, deduped by `requestId`, split per token class — so later phases optimize against real cost weights.

## Relationship to `autopilot-run-accounting`

That roadmap builds token accounting as a **product feature**: pricing in `rdm-core`, a `rdm cost` command, run records as plan-repo artifacts. This roadmap builds only a **repo-local measurement harness** sized to gate reduction work, deliberately narrower and following the `scripts/verify-*.sh` convention. Where the two overlap, `autopilot-run-accounting` is authoritative and this harness is expected to be superseded.

## Evidence already gathered

A controlled A/B (8 findings x {Opus, Sonnet} x 2 replicates, identical `refutePrompt` input, only the model varying) found:

- **7/8 majority agreement**, with **zero within-model verdict flips** across replicates — refutation is stable, not stochastic.
- **Sonnet is not cheaper in tokens** (52.9k avg vs Opus 48.4k). Any saving from re-tiering is price-per-token, not volume.
- The single disagreement was the case that matters: a finding that was mechanically true but not a defect. Opus found the governing changelog entry and harness acceptance criterion and refuted; Sonnet verified the mechanical fact and stopped, which would have surfaced a false positive and triggered a wasted rework round.
- The ~48% production refutation rate is **not waste**. Three findings planted as genuine defects were correctly refuted by both models with substantive arguments — the refute stage is catching the mechanically-true-but-not-a-defect class, which is most of what plan-stage review produces.

Reduction should therefore come from **fewer agents**, not cheaper agents.

## Explicitly out of scope

Threading the diff into finder prompts was investigated and rejected. `buildDiffSignalsPrompt` truncates `diffText` to 40,000 characters, and `DIFF_SIGNALS_SCHEMA` documents that the truncation is only safe because it degrades toward fail-open for *trigger detection*. Feeding that truncated blob to finders as review material inverts the property — finders would silently review a partial diff. A narrower variant passing only `changedFiles` may be revisited, but is not planned here.
planDoc:
Cut token consumption in the `.claude/workflows/` autonomous lane, measuring every change against a committed baseline rather than against intuition.

## Why

A survey of the 20 lane runs on disk (autopilot / dispatch-phase / plan-review / backlog / estimate) found spend concentrated in review, not implementation:

| class | agents | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| review — find | 366 | 37% |
| review — refute | 492 | 36% |
| mechanical (fetch/stamp/estimate/diff) | 191 | 11% |
| implement | 37 | 8% |
| plan author/revise | 53 | 6% |

Review outweighs implementation ~8.6:1. A linear fit of tokens against tool calls gives an intercept of ~36.8k tokens per agent before any work is done, and the cheapest agent observed cost 27k — so a large fraction of lane spend is per-agent context loading, repeated across 1,156 agents. `CLAUDE.md` (~11.7k tokens) plus the user-global one (~3.3k) is loaded into every one of them, including agents whose entire job is running a single `rdm` command.

## Measurement caveat this roadmap must fix first

Those figures come from `workflowProgress[].tokens` and `totalTokens` in the session sidecars. The sibling `autopilot-run-accounting` roadmap establishes from a measured run that those fields are **not a cost basis**: they do not reconcile with deduped per-class totals and omit cache reads entirely (36.7M cache reads in a run whose non-cache-read classes summed to 4.4M). The class *ranking* above is believed sound; the absolute totals understate traffic and are blind to any change that trades cache-write for cache-read.

Phase 1 therefore re-derives the baseline from the `agent-*.jsonl` transcripts, deduped by `requestId`, split per token class — so later phases optimize against real cost weights.

## Relationship to `autopilot-run-accounting`

That roadmap builds token accounting as a **product feature**: pricing in `rdm-core`, a `rdm cost` command, run records as plan-repo artifacts. This roadmap builds only a **repo-local measurement harness** sized to gate reduction work, deliberately narrower and following the `scripts/verify-*.sh` convention. Where the two overlap, `autopilot-run-accounting` is authoritative and this harness is expected to be superseded.

## Evidence already gathered

A controlled A/B (8 findings x {Opus, Sonnet} x 2 replicates, identical `refutePrompt` input, only the model varying) found:

- **7/8 majority agreement**, with **zero within-model verdict flips** across replicates — refutation is stable, not stochastic.
- **Sonnet is not cheaper in tokens** (52.9k avg vs Opus 48.4k). Any saving from re-tiering is price-per-token, not volume.
- The single disagreement was the case that matters: a finding that was mechanically true but not a defect. Opus found the governing changelog entry and harness acceptance criterion and refuted; Sonnet verified the mechanical fact and stopped, which would have surfaced a false positive and triggered a wasted rework round.
- The ~48% production refutation rate is **not waste**. Three findings planted as genuine defects were correctly refuted by both models with substantive arguments — the refute stage is catching the mechanically-true-but-not-a-defect class, which is most of what plan-stage review produces.

Reduction should therefore come from **fewer agents**, not cheaper agents.

## Explicitly out of scope

Threading the diff into finder prompts was investigated and rejected. `buildDiffSignalsPrompt` truncates `diffText` to 40,000 characters, and `DIFF_SIGNALS_SCHEMA` documents that the truncation is only safe because it degrades toward fail-open for *trigger detection*. Feeding that truncated blob to finders as review material inverts the property — finders would silently review a partial diff. A narrower variant passing only `changedFiles` may be revisited, but is not planned here.

coherence.concern: Phases 3, 4 and 6 all edit workflow scripts that have hand-synced byte-identical copies embedded in the rdm-core crate, but no phase's steps or acceptance criteria mention syncing them or running the harness that gates them.
coherence.location: phase-3-trim-mechanical-agent-context (steps 6, 9; ACs 5-7), phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation (steps 6, 8; AC 7), phase-6-halting-token-budget (steps 1, 7; AC 1)
coherence.what_fails: Phase 3 modifies `.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js` and `autopilot.js`; phase 4 restamps `review.mjs` into `review-refute-fix.js`, `dispatch-phase.js` and `plan-review.js`; phase 6 modifies `autopilot.js` and `dispatch-phase.js`. Three of those files exist a second time at `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` (verified `cmp`-identical today, `include_str!`'d at `rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs:355-363`) and are gated for byte-identity by `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` section 3. These copies are NOT produced by `gen-workflow-review.sh` or any other generator — they are hand-maintained. Phase 3 step 6 covers only 'its generator so the stamped copies stay byte-identical' (lib -> workflow .js), phase 3 AC 5 covers only 'the existing byte-identity generators and their `--check` gates', and phase 4 step 6 covers only the two review generators. An implementer following any of these phases as written regenerates the lib->js stamping, sees those `--check` gates pass, and never touches the crate copies.
coherence.why: The plan is otherwise scrupulous about single-source/projection contracts (phase 4 step 6 enumerates both review generators in both modes; phase 3 AC 5 names the byte-identity gates), so the omission reads as an oversight rather than a deliberate scope boundary. Its consequence is concrete: `verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` fails in CI, or — if the phase's own harness list is trusted and that script is not run — `rdm agent-config claude --skills` ships downstream repos a lane that is a full roadmap behind, quietly forfeiting every saving these phases measure. Phase 3 in particular has a caller-side half (step 2's skill-shim hoist) whose distributed counterpart lives in `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-{autopilot,dispatch-phase,do}-{cli,mcp}.md`, also unmentioned.
coherence.recommendation: Add to phases 3, 4 and 6 an explicit step to re-sync `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/*.js` from `.claude/workflows/*.js` (and, for phase 3, the `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-*.md` shim templates), plus an acceptance criterion that `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` passes. Alternatively state once in the roadmap body that crate-copy re-sync is a standing obligation of every phase that touches a distributed workflow script.

coherence.concern: Phase 5 declares historical findings unrecoverable from run records citing only the sidecar preview truncation, contradicting Phase 1's own data model and undercutting Phase 4's acceptance criterion, which requires exactly that recovery.
coherence.location: phase-5-refuter-model-tiering-decision step 3 and step 2; phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation step 5 and AC 6
coherence.what_fails: Phase 5 step 3: 'Note the constraint that `promptPreview` and `resultPreview` in the sidecars are hard-truncated to 401 characters, so historical findings cannot be replayed verbatim from run records — the corpus must be constructed or captured live.' The premise is about the `wf_*.json` sidecars only. Phase 1 of this same roadmap establishes a second, full-fidelity source and builds a parser for it: `subagents/workflows/<runId>/agent-*.jsonl`. I checked a real one on disk — the refuter's initiating user turn carries the complete 5,607-character prompt, not a 401-character preview, and the assistant turns carry the full structured verdict. Historical refuter prompt/verdict pairs are therefore recoverable at full fidelity. Meanwhile Phase 4 step 5 instructs 'Measure how many production `concern` findings were refuted in the historical runs' and Phase 4 AC 6 hard-requires 'The `concern` disposition is decided from measured historical refutation rates' — satisfiable only via the transcript recovery Phase 5 says is impossible.
coherence.why: An implementer taking phase 5 step 3 at face value hand-constructs the whole corpus against 'known repo facts' rather than mining the 20 runs on disk, in a phase whose entire premise is that eight items is too small a sample and that the mechanically-true-but-not-a-defect class must be over-represented. Synthetic items cannot establish the production distribution the phase needs. Symmetrically, a phase-4 implementer who reads phase 5 first may conclude AC 6 is unmeetable and either block or fabricate a rate. This is not a citation error — both statements are internally reasonable — but they cannot both guide the same corpus decision.
coherence.recommendation: Rewrite phase 5 step 3 to scope the truncation claim to the `wf_*.json` sidecars and state that full prompts and verdicts ARE recoverable from `agent-*.jsonl` transcripts via the phase-1 parser, making transcript mining the primary corpus source with construction as the top-up. Cross-reference that source from phase 4 step 5 so its measurement has a named method.

coherence.concern: Phase 4's closing acceptance criterion demands a measured drop in refuter agent count using a metric Phase 2 itself documents as non-comparable across runs, and provides no negative-result path even though its own step 5 may legitimately decide to keep refuting the dominant severity class.
coherence.location: phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation AC 10 ('Refuter agent count and token share drop against docs/token-baseline.json, with the measured delta recorded'), read against phase-2-baseline-snapshot step 6 / AC 6 and phase-4 step 5
coherence.what_fails: Phase 2 AC 6 requires documenting that 'runs differ in roadmap size, phase difficulty, and rework rounds, so per-run totals are not directly comparable — per-agent-class and per-phase-dispatch figures are.' Refuter agent count is a direct function of how many findings the finders produced, which varies with roadmap size and phase count — precisely the confound. An implementer can satisfy AC 10 by dispatching a smaller roadmap post-change and reporting a 'drop' that is entirely selection effect. Separately, step 5 leaves `concern` open ('if the refutation rate is high, keep refuting them and record why'). In plan mode only `blocking` gates (`classifyPlanOutcome`; `lib/review.mjs:393` — 'reviewed — clean, or clean with recorded concerns/suggestions'), and the plan-stage severity contract routes most concrete defects to `concern`, so a 'keep refuting concerns' decision leaves suggestions-only as the skipped class and the drop could be near zero — yet AC 10 mandates a drop unconditionally.
coherence.why: Phases 3 and 5 both handle exactly this risk explicitly (phase 3 AC: 'If it does not drop, the negative result is recorded and the change is reverted rather than kept on faith'; phase 5 step 7: 'a measured negative result is the deliverable'). Phase 4's omission is inconsistent with its siblings and creates pressure to either pick a flattering comparison or to override step 5's evidence-driven `concern` decision in order to close the phase.
coherence.recommendation: Restate AC 10 in a confound-resistant unit — refuters per finding, or refuters per phase dispatch, normalized as Phase 2 AC 6 prescribes — and add the sibling escape hatch: if the step-5 evidence keeps `concern` refuted and the residual saving is negligible, that negative result is a legitimate completion, recorded rather than engineered away.

coherence.concern: Phase 3 makes passing a custom `agentType` an unconditional acceptance criterion while its own step 4 treats the option's existence as something still to be confirmed, and the repo's documented Workflow runtime surface does not list it.
coherence.location: phase-3-trim-mechanical-agent-context, 'Lever 2 — trim what remains' and step 4 vs AC 4
coherence.what_fails: Step 4 says 'Follow whatever registry mechanism `agentType` resolves against, and confirm it is reachable from the Workflow runtime before building on it' — an explicit acknowledgement that reachability is unverified. AC 4 then states flatly: 'Every mechanical `agent()` call site that remains passes the mechanical `agentType` and `effort: 'low'`.' `docs/workflow-schemas.md` enumerates the runtime's entire global scope (line 66) and documents `agent()` options only for `opts.model`, settled by a named 5-case empirical spike that read `message.model` out of transcripts rather than trusting acceptance; neither `agentType` nor `effort` appears anywhere in that document, and `grep` confirms neither is used under `.claude/workflows/`. If the step-4 spike shows `agentType` is silently ignored (the exact failure mode that spike guards against — an option accepted but inert, as `model: undefined` was found to be), AC 4 becomes unsatisfiable with no recorded alternative.
coherence.why: The roadmap's stated discipline is to measure rather than assume, and phase 3 applies it correctly elsewhere: step 5's `CLAUDE.md` question has a matching negative-result AC ('answered empirically and written down'), and the token-floor AC reverts on no improvement. The `agentType` lever has the verification step but not the matching escape, so a spike returning 'not honored' leaves the phase with an AC that cannot be closed honestly.
coherence.recommendation: Make AC 4 conditional on the step-4 spike, mirroring the CLAUDE.md AC: require that whether the Workflow runtime honors `agentType` and `effort` is answered empirically and written down, and that every remaining mechanical call site carries whichever of the two is honored. Optionally add the spike to step 4 as a named deliverable in the style of the `opts.model` spike table already in `docs/workflow-schemas.md`.

architectural-fit.concern: Phases 3, 4 and 6 all edit `.claude/workflows/lib/*.mjs` and re-stamp the workflow consumers, but no phase accounts for the hand-maintained byte-identical copies at `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` — nor for the distributed skill templates under `rdm-core/src/templates/`. Nothing regenerates those copies, so the plan as written lands the repo in a CI-failing state.
architectural-fit.location: phase-3-trim-mechanical-agent-context (steps 2, 6; ACs "existing byte-identity generators and their --check gates pass"), phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation (step 6; AC "every stamped consumer and skill template is regenerated"), phase-6-halting-token-budget (steps 1-5)
architectural-fit.what_fails: Phase 3 modifies `lib/dispatch-phase.mjs` and `lib/autopilot.mjs`; phase 4 modifies `lib/review.mjs` (stamped into `dispatch-phase.js` and `review-refute-fix.js`); phase 6 modifies `lib/autopilot.mjs` and `lib/dispatch-phase.mjs`. Each re-stamp mutates one or more of exactly the three files that `rdm-core/src/agent_config.rs:355-363` embeds via `include_str!("templates/workflows/...")`. Verified on `main`: `diff -q .claude/workflows/<f> rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/<f>` is currently identical for all three, and `grep -n templates scripts/gen-workflow-review.sh` shows the generator never writes to `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` (its only `templates` reference is a comment about *skill* templates; `gen-workflow-estimate.sh` has none, and there is no `build.rs`). So after any of these phases, `.claude/workflows/*.js` and its shipped copy diverge, and two CI-listed harnesses hard-fail: `scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh:88` (`diff -q "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/workflows/$name" "$dir/.claude/workflows/$name"` over `WORKFLOWS="autopilot.js dispatch-phase.js review-refute-fix.js"`, line 74) and `scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh:79` (`WF_TEMPLATE=.../templates/workflows/review-refute-fix.js`). CLAUDE.md's CI block runs `for f in scripts/verify-*.sh; do bash "$f"; done`, so both are gating. Phase 3 step 2 additionally says "update the parent skill shim to gather and pass it" without distinguishing `.claude/skills/` (dogfooding copies) from `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-{autopilot,dispatch-phase}-{cli,mcp}.md` / `skill-do-{cli,mcp}.md` (the distributed surface that `verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `verify-workflow-do-auto{,-task}.sh` gate).
architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md states the distribution contract explicitly: `rdm agent-config claude --skills --out <dir>` emits the three `.claude/workflows/*.js` scripts "embedded via `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/` ... byte-identical to this repo's own `.claude/workflows/` copies", and describes `verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` as gating exactly that byte-identity. Every phase's acceptance criteria enumerate the gates they must satisfy (`gen-workflow-review.sh --check`, `gen-skill-review.sh --check` in both modes, `§5b-mechanical`, the per-lib drift gates) — the omission of the Rust-embedded copies is conspicuous against that level of enumeration, not an oversight the ACs implicitly cover, since those ACs speak only of "stamped consumers" and the stamping generators demonstrably do not reach the templates directory.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Add an explicit step and acceptance criterion to phases 3, 4 and 6: after re-running the stamping generators, re-sync `rdm-core/src/templates/workflows/{autopilot,dispatch-phase,review-refute-fix}.js` from `.claude/workflows/`, and require `bash scripts/verify-agent-config-distribution.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-workflow-review-outcome.sh` to pass. For phase 3's hoist, name `rdm-core/src/templates/skill-{autopilot,dispatch-phase}-{cli,mcp}.md` and the `--auto` section of `skill-do-{cli,mcp}.md` as the surfaces to edit, with `.claude/skills/` regenerated to match. Consider filing the missing automation (a `gen-workflow-templates.sh --check`, or teaching `gen-workflow-review.sh` to copy) as a side-task rather than leaving a third manual byte-identity contract.

architectural-fit.concern: Phase 3 nominates `stamp:in-progress` as the likeliest absorption target on the premise that "the implementer agent is spawned moments later". It is not — the implementer runs after the entire plan-author/plan-review/revise gate, and does not run at all when the plan gate escalates. Absorbing the stamp there would regress the documented `no-in-progress-stamp` invariant.
architectural-fit.location: phase-3-trim-mechanical-agent-context — "Lever 1 ... Can an agent that is already running absorb it?" bullet, and step 3 ("most likely `stamp:in-progress` into the implementer's prompt")
architectural-fit.what_fails: In `.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js` the `stamp:in-progress` agent (line 1626) is emitted immediately after Stage 0 model resolution and *before* `runPlanGate` — its own comment reads "mark the item in-progress the moment real work begins (right after Stage 0 resolves metadata + models, before planning)". Between that stamp and the implementer sit `plan:author`, the full `buildReviewPipeline('plan')` fan-out (finders + a refuter per finding), and up to `maxPlanRevise` `plan:revise` rounds — by this roadmap's own figures the most expensive stretch of the pipeline, not "moments". Worse, the stamped `classifyOutcome` contract (dispatch-phase.js line ~778: "Plan gate: a blocking plan finding escalates before any implementation") means a plan-gate escalation never reaches the implementer, so an absorbed stamp would leave that item going `not-started` → `blocked` with no in-progress signal at all — precisely the gap CLAUDE.md's "Update (no-in-progress-stamp)" says was closed. Phase 3's AC ("the in-progress stamp still being observable during a dispatch") does not catch this, because it does not constrain *when* the stamp lands or cover the plan-escalation path.
architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md's "Update (no-in-progress-stamp)" is a stated design decision with an explicitly recorded rationale: the stamp is a best-effort mechanical write "right after Stage 0 (metadata + model resolution) and before planning begins", added because a direct `Workflow` invocation "used to jump straight from `not-started` to a terminal status with no observable in-progress signal during the run". Deferring it into the implementer reintroduces that condition on the escalation path and materially delays it on the happy path. The phase does hedge ("Weigh this against the reason the split exists ... Record the trade-off per call site rather than applying the rewrite blindly"), but the false timing premise is what makes this call site look like the obvious win, so the hedge is unlikely to bite.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Correct the premise in the phase body (the implementer is separated from Stage 0 by the whole plan gate, and does not run on a plan-gate escalation), and either drop `stamp:in-progress` from the absorption candidates or require the analysis in step 1 to record the plan-escalation path explicitly. If it is kept as a candidate, strengthen the AC to "the item is observably `in-progress` before the plan gate runs, including on a run that escalates at the plan gate" so the invariant is tested rather than assumed. Note that the parallel `diff:signals` absorption into the implementer has no such ordering problem and is the safer of the two.

architectural-fit.concern: No phase mentions `CHANGELOG.md`, yet phases 3, 4 and 6 change the observable behavior of the skills and workflows that `rdm agent-config` ships, and phase 6 adds a new configuration surface.
architectural-fit.location: phase-3-trim-mechanical-agent-context, phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation, phase-6-halting-token-budget — Steps and Acceptance Criteria
architectural-fit.what_fails: Phase 4 changes the shipped skill templates (`skill-review-{cli,mcp}.md`, `skill-plan-review-{cli,mcp}.md` via `gen-skill-review.sh`) and alters what the review pipeline hands to the receiving agent; phase 6 adds an operator-facing token budget and its configuration surface (step 6: "Decide and document where the budget is configured — Workflow args, rdm config, or both"); phase 3 changes the `args` contract of distributed workflows. Each is a user-facing change under CLAUDE.md's definition ("CLI commands, API endpoints, MCP tools, config options, or observable behavior"). None of the eighteen-odd acceptance criteria across those three phases requires a changelog entry.
architectural-fit.why: CLAUDE.md states: "**Every commit with a user-facing change MUST include a corresponding `CHANGELOG.md` update in the same commit.** Do not defer changelog entries to a later commit or batch them up." This is not merely a house style here — the lane's own code-review pipeline encodes it as a gating rule (`.claude/workflows/dispatch-phase.js:155`: "A user-facing change ... MUST carry a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] in the SAME commit — a missing entry is a `blocking` finding per CLAUDE.md"), so a phase that omits it will be self-blocked by its own dispatch and burn a rework round — an ironic cost in a roadmap whose subject is lane spend.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Add a `CHANGELOG.md` step and acceptance criterion to phases 3, 4 and 6 (phase 6's should name the new budget configuration surface and its default of "no budget"). Phases 1, 2 and 5 are repo-local tooling/docs and can state explicitly that no changelog entry is warranted, so the omission reads as a decision rather than a gap.

architectural-fit.concern: Phase 1 introduces a checked-in fixture tree at `tests/fixtures/token-sidecar/`, a directory shape that does not exist anywhere in this workspace and that diverges from the established `verify-*.sh` convention of hermetic seeding.
architectural-fit.location: phase-1-token-measurement-harness — step 5 and the AC "passes hermetically against the checked-in fixture"
architectural-fit.what_fails: There is no `tests/` directory at the workspace root and no `fixtures/` or `testdata/` directory anywhere in the repo (verified by `find` excluding `target/`). Every existing harness — `verify-workflow-{review,dispatch,autopilot,estimate,backlog,document}.sh`, `verify-backlog-groom-loop.sh`, `verify-claude-code-web-loop.sh` — seeds its own state into a temp dir at run time, several of them driving the real `./target/debug/rdm` binary. A root-level `tests/` in a cargo workspace whose root has no lib target is also inert to cargo, which invites the misreading that it is a Rust test directory.
architectural-fit.why: Not a violation of a stated constraint, so not a gate — but the roadmap body itself claims this harness "follow[s] the `scripts/verify-*.sh` convention", and a checked-in fixture tree in a new top-level directory is the one place it does not.
architectural-fit.recommendation: Either seed the sidecar fixture from the harness at run time (matching the other harnesses, and keeping the AC's "touching no real `~/.claude` data" guarantee trivially true), or place the fixture under `scripts/fixtures/token-sidecar/` next to the existing `scripts/lib/`, which is where the harness that consumes it lives. Separately, phase 1 step 7 says "Add the harness to the CI list in `CLAUDE.md`" — that list is already the glob `for f in scripts/verify-*.sh`, so the real edit is the per-harness prose list in the Dogfooding section; worth restating so the implementer edits the right block.

restraint.concern: The roadmap body's "Evidence already gathered" A/B results are restated near-verbatim inside phase 5's Context (and the same narrative again in phase 4's Context), while phase 2 step 3 instructs the implementer to update only the roadmap body when the measured numbers revise the survey. The evidence is specified in more places than the plan has a mechanism to keep in sync.
restraint.location: roadmap workflow-token-reduction body, "Evidence already gathered"; phase-5-refuter-model-tiering-decision Context; phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation Context; phase-2-baseline-snapshot step 3
restraint.what_fails: The roadmap body says "Sonnet is not cheaper in tokens (52.9k avg vs Opus 48.4k)", "7/8 majority agreement, with zero within-model verdict flips", and the Opus-vs-Sonnet disagreement narrative. Phase 5 Context repeats all three ("Sonnet was not cheaper in tokens — 52.9k average against Opus 48.4k", "7/8 majority agreement; zero within-model verdict flips", the same 13-20 vs 7-9 tool-call story), and phase 4 Context repeats the refutation-is-real-work argument again. Phase 2 step 3 says "say so plainly and update the roadmap body" — nothing directs an update to the phase copies, and phases 3/4 additionally hard-code the `tokens`-field figures the roadmap itself declares non-authoritative (191 agents ~11%, 492 agents ~36%, 366 ~37%). After phase 2 lands a corrected baseline, the roadmap body is updated and three phase bodies silently retain superseded numbers that the implementing agents of phases 3-5 will read as current.
restraint.why: This is the second restraint shape: detail replicated past the point where it reduces risk. One authoritative statement of the A/B evidence plus a pointer from each phase would carry the same information with one copy to maintain; the current arrangement adds three more documents to review and to keep true, and phase 2's own update instruction proves the maintenance burden was only partly noticed.
restraint.recommendation: Keep the A/B evidence and the survey table in exactly one place (the roadmap body, since phase 2 is already charged with revising it) and have phases 3-5 reference it ("see the roadmap body's Evidence section") rather than restating figures. If the phase copies are kept deliberately, widen phase 2 step 3 to require updating every place the superseded figures appear, so the plan's own consistency rule matches its duplication.

restraint.concern: Phase 4 writes the production prompt sentence for un-refuted suggestions four times — in Context, in step 4, in shorthand in step 8, and again in the acceptance criterion — each a slightly different paraphrase of the same rule.
restraint.location: phase-4-skip-non-gating-refutation, Context paragraph 4; steps 4 and 8; acceptance criterion 5
restraint.what_fails: Context: "incorporate suggestions that improve readability or clarity where doing so does not require a major change; skip the rest and say why" plus a definition of "major". Step 4: "incorporate the ones that improve readability or clarity where the change is not major, skip the rest with a stated reason, and treat anything that would change the approach, widen scope, or reach outside the diff as follow-up". AC 5: a third paraphrase. Step 8: "the incorporate-if-not-major instruction". The three long paraphrases are not byte-identical, so an implementer transcribing the rule into the stamped block has to decide which phrasing is authoritative, and a later edit to one paraphrase leaves the other two contradicting it inside the same document.
restraint.why: Restraint shape (2): stating the rule once is load-bearing (the wording ships into the prompt); stating it three more times in near-but-not-quite-identical form adds review surface and internal-consistency risk without adding constraint.
restraint.recommendation: State the disposition rule once as a quoted block (the wording that should land in the stamped prompt), and have step 4, step 8, and the acceptance criterion refer to it by name rather than re-paraphrasing it.

restraint.concern: Phase 1 specifies implementation details that no acceptance criterion checks and that the implementer could safely choose — the exact CLI flag surface and the fixture's file count.
restraint.location: phase-1-token-measurement-harness, steps 3 and 5
restraint.what_fails: Step 3 fixes four flags (`--since <iso-date>`, `--workflow <name>` repeatable, `--format text|json`, `--out <path>`); none appear in the phase's acceptance criteria, and phase 2 step 1 only requires that the CLI can be run across the on-disk runs, not that it takes any particular flag. Step 5 says "two or three `agent-*.jsonl` files" — a count the ACs do not constrain and that cannot be satisfied wrongly. restraint.why: Restraint shape (1): the plan spells out decisions that could be left to whoever carries them out. The load-bearing constraints in this phase (stdlib-only, dedupe by `requestId`, per-token-class breakdown, worktree-directory search, planted-mutation self-test) are already stated as ACs; the flag list and fixture count add detail below the level at which the plan is gating anything.
